A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #5206: "use database" handling in mysql CLI client broken

Issue description:
The mysql CLI client transforms commands of the form:   "USE database1" to a COM_INIT_DB MySQL RPC against the server.

However, I suspect a recent change (#5136) broke this handling.  The result is that issuing a "USE keyspace1" request against vtgate will succeed and have the desired result the first time, but thereafter, "USE keyspace2" will seem to succeed, but not actually change the keyspace/DB context.

Using a client (e.g. the python MySQLdb module) that does not issue COM_INIT_DB, and insteads sends "USE keyspaceX" as a query, seems to still work properly.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: mysql: handle db name correctly
PR description:
Fixes #5206

The conn schemaname var can get set through a new connection
or a ComInitDB packet. However, a use statement bypasses this
mechanism and gets handled at the vtgate level. This causes
problems because schemaName in the connection disagrees with
TargetString in vtgate.

To fix this, the new scheme calls a new handler function: ComInitDB
every time schemaName is initialized or changed in the connection.
This way, the TargetString remains the authoritative source
for the current db name.

I couldn't write a test for this specific behavior change because
the mysql go client does not implement support for ComInitDB.
But I've verified the things generally work as expected.

Signed-off-by: Sugu Sougoumarane <ssougou@gmail.com>

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Make semi sync extension optional
PR description:
Fixes https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/issues/4762

There is a use case to attach Vitess to an existing MySQL topology and then migrate into Vitess. Currently this requires the semi sync extension to be present (irrespective of whether semi-sync is used). This is because of the way the mysql server handles config options: the plugins register them with the server. If the plugin is not present, there is an error because the option is unknown.

Since a user may be moving from a managed platform, or may not want to make too many changes to the source, it is important to not error if semi-sync commands can not be executed.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #5760: Parse check constraints

Issue description:
#### Feature Description

When creating a table in MySQL, a number of [check constraints](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-table-check-constraints.html) can be added.

```
CREATE TABLE t1
(
  CHECK (c1 <> c2),
  c1 INT CHECK (c1 > 10),
  c2 INT CONSTRAINT c2_positive CHECK (c2 > 0),
  c3 INT CHECK (c3 < 100),
  CONSTRAINT c1_nonzero CHECK (c1 <> 0),
  CHECK (c1 > c3)
);
```

The sqlparser module does not currently parse these statements.

#### Use Case(s)

sqlparser is being used by https://github.com/kyleconroy/sqlc, a SQL to Go code generator, and needs this information to correctly generate code from database migrations and other code using CHECK constraints.

PR title: Use DesiredState.Host in scheduler predicate
PR description:
This is an attempt to fix #1751

Method MapPodsToMachines always returns a map of empty host to a list of pods, thus when passing existing pods to predicate, predicate will always get an empty list.  In this case, all predicates will return true, even if there is an existing port conflict. If we get unlucky, the node that has the highest priority (least used resources) is the node has port conflict, then scheduler will do a retry but still use the same wrong node.

The problems seems to be that MapPodsToMachines use CurrentState.Host, which is only set in GetPod and ListPods.  However, Scheduler uses a PodLister, which is a podCache using Reflector (List and Watch).  After initial List, podCache will watch on Pod changs, which won't have the CurrentState.Host correctly set.

This is what I've diagonsed so far, the problem seems to go away (Run 200+ times without error).  However, I believe there is a reason for using CurrentState, if so, then this may not be the right fix.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2358: Exposing services outside the cluster (or in different parts of the cluster) to pods

Issue description:
Today, we have a solution for abstracting a set of pods on a single port to other pods called a `service`.  A service hides the details of location, load balancing, and placement, and provides a stable endpoint that other pods may access.  A service also provides simple discovery via environment variables injected into pods.  A service may be bound accessible from the outside of a cluster via infrastructure load balancing.

There are other resources that pods must access:
- Services outside the cluster like infrastructure databases, SaaS endpoints, internet providers
- Services that exist in other clusters, other namespaces within the same cluster, or as an aggregation of services.

These `external services` (working term only) may cross network, security, or policy boundaries, but to a pod consumer they are all network available resources on a port.  If a service has multiple endpoints, it may wish a pod consumer to be able to transparently load balance those endpoints.

At the current time, Kubernetes exposes the master as a virtual service on startup to other services by pretending to be a pod service and updating its own endpoints.  The master may not always run in a pod, but it would still be valuable to expose itself to discovery by pods.  Other consumers may need to do similarly.

Finally, each service has a list of endpoints that are maintained by the endpoints controller, which resolves the service pod selector, determines the IP of the available pods, and exposes them to consumers like the kube-proxy.  There is no way for a service author to instruct the endpoints controller to bypass his endpoints so he may manage them himself.

Possible avenues that could address these needs:
1. Expose a new resource that exposes the discovery and proxy behavior of services, but has no label selector (thus is does not select pods, but something else).  It would be able to have different schema than services.
   - Objects would be different, but have similar effect.  Portal IPs have to be reserved across a homogenous set, so both resources would try to pull from the same pool.
2. On a service, allow a consumer to indicate that the label selector is irrelevant, and a separate process could manage the endpoints.  Consumers would need to create a service and then set endpoints directly (in two separate calls).  Services would no longer to be guaranteed to be about pods.
   - suggested by lavalamp: "a flag called externallyManaged"
3. Split the service discovery and proxy behavior of a service from the backend behavior of a service (variant of both 1 and 2), and offer more tuning of the service.  Service discovery and the portal would be the same for all services, but the backend would differ.
   - e.g. lavalamp's suggestion below

Other thoughts:
- External services often come with additional data that govern their use.  By far the most common is a username and password (or security token and context) that govern their use (see Heroku Add-ons). These attributes are present only when the external service is used, but if the external service is removed it would be reasonable to remove them.  It might be valuable to add environment variables with a service that expose with that service portal.

Issue #2623: kube-proxy continuously adding entries to iptables

Issue description:
I am running kubernetes 0.5.2 + [patch to support older iptables](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/pull/2067) and I've noticed that the number of entries in iptables increases every few seconds.

I started with a clean install, no pods or replicationControllers, there is now two services by default (kubernetes-ro and kubernetes). I ran `iptables-save | wc -l` and got `38`.

Next, I turned up 7 services and 3 replicationControllers which resulted in 3 pods also being turned up.

I started a watch...

```
watch 'iptables-save | wc -l'
```

I saw "38", "43, "50, "64", "66", "68", "70", ..., "115" ...on and on until I stopped `kube-proxy`. It appears the proxy continues to add REDIRECT's for the services, for example the lines that keep being added look like:

`-A KUBE-PROXY -d 10.254.178.203/32 -p tcp -m comment --comment "kubernetes" -m tcp --dport 443 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 56052`

A similar line for each service gets added every second or so, it appears to all be in the `nat` table. I'm thinking the newly added [checkRuleWithoutCheck](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/util/iptables/iptables.go#L191) function might be the culprit, since [EnsureRule](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/util/iptables/iptables.go#L118) calls `checkRule` and in the `kube-proxy` log I see [running iptables -A ...](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/util/iptables/iptables.go#L169) every few seconds (looks like [proxier.go](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/proxy/proxier.go#L344) does a sync every 5 seconds).

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Fix iptables for old systems
PR description:
The iptables args list needs to include all fields as they are eventually spit
out by iptables-save.  This is because some systems do not support the
'iptables -C' arg, and so fall back on parsing iptables-save output.  If this
does not match, it will not pass the check.  For example: adding the /32 on
the destination IP arg is not strictly required, but causes this list to not
match the final iptables-save output.  This is fragile and I hope one day we
can stop supporting such old iptables versions.

@hmrm @mindscratch

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2495: Kubelet doesn't kill old pods when BoundPods is empty

Issue description:
To reproduce:
- Start a cluster via hack/local-up-cluster.sh
- Start some pods
- Kill the cluster
- "docker ps -a" should show the pod containers running still
- Start the cluster again
- "etcdctl ls /registry" should show that there is no boundpods directory -- only minions and services
- "docker ps -a" should show the old pod containers still running
- Start a new pod
- After, say, 10s, "docker ps -a" should show the old containers dead

/cc @dchen1107

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Fix "Kubelet doesn't kill old pods when BoundPods is empty" issue
PR description:
Fixes #2495: **Kubelet doesn't kill old pods when BoundPods is empty**

The first time kubelet starts, while there are no updates, `kl.pods` is `nil` ([pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1118](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1118)):

``` GO
case <-time.After(kl.resyncInterval):
    glog.V(4).Infof("Periodic sync")
    if kl.pods == nil {
        continue
    }
```

which guarantees that [`syncPods(...)`](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L992), which contains the container killing logic is never called.

So the first part of the fix is to remove this check and allow `syncPods(...)` to be called even when nil, so that the first periodic sync can clean up old containers.

However, this isn't enough because inside `syncPods(...)` there is a check to make sure that all sources have been "seen" before it will kill old containers ([pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1026](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1026)):

``` GO
if !kl.sourcesReady() {
    // If the sources aren't ready, skip deletion, as we may accidentally delete pods
    // for sources that haven't reported yet.
    glog.V(4).Infof("Skipping deletes, sources aren't ready yet.")
    return nil
}
```

This check is performed in the [`SeenAllSources()`](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L87) function, and is `true` only if a `SET` update has been seen for all registered kubelet sources.

However, no `SET` update is emitted by any of the sources until they successfully read a value, which means the original problem still exists.

So the second part of the fix is to have the kubelet boundpod sources (etcd, file, and http) all emit a `SET` update with an empty pod list when the source is first read but no value exists; the empty update will not make it back to the kubelet sync loop because it will be filtered out by the [update merge logic](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L140); but it will cause the source to be [marked as seen](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L238) so the periodic sync (enabled by the first fix) will clean up the old containers (since all sources will now be marked as seen after the first read attempt).

The first time kubelet starts, while there are no updates, `kl.pods` is `nil` ([pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1118](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1118)):

``` GO
case <-time.After(kl.resyncInterval):
    glog.V(4).Infof("Periodic sync")
    if kl.pods == nil {
        continue
    }
```

which guarantees that [`syncPods(...)`](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L992), which contains the container killing logic is never called.

So the first part of the fix is to remove this check and allow `syncPods(...)` to be called even when nil, so that the first periodic sync can clean up old containers.

However, this isn't enough because inside `syncPods(...)` there is a check to make sure that all sources have been "seen" before it will kill old containers ([pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1026](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1026)):

``` GO
if !kl.sourcesReady() {
    // If the sources aren't ready, skip deletion, as we may accidentally delete pods
    // for sources that haven't reported yet.
    glog.V(4).Infof("Skipping deletes, sources aren't ready yet.")
    return nil
}
```

This check is performed in the [`SeenAllSources()`](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L87) function, and is `true` only if a `SET` update has been seen for all registered kubelet sources.

However, no `SET` update is emitted by any of the sources until they successfully read a value, which means the original problem still exists.

So the second part of the fix is to have the kubelet boundpod sources (etcd, file, and http) all emit a `SET` update with an empty pod list when the source is first read but no value exists; the empty update will not make it back to the kubelet sync loop because it will be filtered out by the [update merge logic](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L140); but it will cause the source to be [marked as seen](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L238) so the periodic sync (enabled by the first fix) will clean up the old containers (since all sources will now be marked as seen after the first read attempt).

Issue description:

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2970: Systematically tag readonly API fields

Issue description:
Right now we have haphazard comments regarding which fields are read-only/output-only, and many, such as `uid` aren't documented at all.

Swagger 2.0 actually supports a `readOnly` property tag, but we're using Swagger 1.2, which does not, officially. The official meaning doesn't match what we want, though. `readOnly` fields must not be included in a PUT, which would be painful for clients. We could simply document our convention, however.

We should tag fields as readonly. Maybe we could have go-restful automatically add a comment to the description in that case.

PR title: v1beta1/v1beta2: consistent description for all read-only fields

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #5112: Change GCE to use standalone SaltStack configuration on each node

Issue description:
For GKE, we have a goal of securing the node -> master communication completely, and eliminating it where we can. Rather than head down the rathole of making sure Salt is secure, I decided to look and see how hard it would be just to convert each VM to a standalone SaltStack configuration, ala: http://docs.saltstack.com/en/latest/topics/tutorials/quickstart.html

It turns out, this that isn't hard at all, and completely eliminates node -> master Salt communication. It also spells doom and gloom for any "dynamic configuration story" using Salt, but I fixed up `kube-push` for GCE in the process as well, at least, so there's that.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Change GCE to use standalone Saltstack config
PR description:
Change provisioning to pass all variables to both master and node. Run Salt in a masterless setup on all nodes ala http://docs.saltstack.com/en/latest/topics/tutorials/quickstart.html, which involves ensuring Salt daemon is NOT running after install. Kill Salt master install. And fix push to actually work in this new flow.

As part of this, the GCE Salt config no longer has access to the Salt mine, which is primarily obnoxious for two reasons:
- The minions can't use Salt to see the master: this is easily fixed by static config.
- The master can't see the list of all the minions: this is fixed temporarily by static config in util.sh, but later, by other means (see pieces of #156, which should eventually remove this direction).

Along the way: refactor the node setup/push script(s) in util.sh.

Fixes #5112.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #5327: Event failed to update

Issue description:
Seen in integration test output:

```
E0311 14:09:25.955280   99741 event.go:127] Unable to write event '&api.Event{TypeMeta:api.TypeMeta{Kind:"", APIVersion:""}, ObjectMeta:api.ObjectMeta{Name:"127.0.0.1.13ca8dd23271fd55", GenerateName:"", Namespace:"default", SelfLink:"", UID:"", ResourceVersion:"", CreationTimestamp:util.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:0, nsec:0x0, loc:(*time.Location)(nil)}}, Labels:map[string]string(nil), Annotations:map[string]string(nil)}, InvolvedObject:api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Minion", Namespace:"default", Name:"127.0.0.1", UID:"127.0.0.1", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}, Reason:"starting", Message:"Starting kubelet.", Source:api.EventSource{Component:"kubelet", Host:"127.0.0.1"}, FirstTimestamp:util.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:63561704965, nsec:0x38560b55, loc:(*time.Location)(0x12138e0)}}, LastTimestamp:util.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:63561704965, nsec:0x38560b55, loc:(*time.Location)(0x12138e0)}}, Count:1}': 'events "127.0.0.1.13ca8dd23271fd55" already exists' (will not retry!)
```

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Make each new instance of kubelet generate a new event channel
PR description:
Fixes #5327

Integration test shows a bunch of `Unable to write event` errors:

```
E0311 14:09:25.955280   99741 event.go:127] Unable to write event '&api.Event{TypeMeta:api.TypeMeta{Kind:"", APIVersion:""}, ObjectMeta:api.ObjectMeta{Name:"127.0.0.1.13ca8dd23271fd55", GenerateName:"", Namespace:"default", SelfLink:"", UID:"", ResourceVersion:"", CreationTimestamp:util.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:0, nsec:0x0, loc:(*time.Location)(nil)}}, Labels:map[string]string(nil), Annotations:map[string]string(nil)}, InvolvedObject:api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Minion", Namespace:"default", Name:"127.0.0.1", UID:"127.0.0.1", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}, Reason:"starting", Message:"Starting kubelet.", Source:api.EventSource{Component:"kubelet", Host:"127.0.0.1"}, FirstTimestamp:util.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:63561704965, nsec:0x38560b55, loc:(*time.Location)(0x12138e0)}}, LastTimestamp:util.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:63561704965, nsec:0x38560b55, loc:(*time.Location)(0x12138e0)}}, Count:1}': 'events "127.0.0.1.13ca8dd23271fd55" already exists' (will not retry!)
```

This error, `events ... already exists`, indicates that an event with the same key already exists in etcd.

This happens because the integration test [creates two kubelet instances](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/integration/integration.go#L223) (on two different ports), however the setup process creates two different event listeners that listen to the [same event channel](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/client/record/event.go#L167). Thus, when an event is generated by either instance of kubelet, it is passed through the shared channel, and is [consumed by both instances of kubelet](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/client/record/event.go#L149), both of which [issue calls to the API server to create the same exact event](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/client/record/event.go#L73) in rapid succession (which ever call arrives first, succeeds, and the subsequent call fails with this error). Because etcd is called two times to create the same exact event it returns this error.

The fix ensures that each instance of kubelet creates its own event channel (`EventBroadcaster`) (instead of reusing existing).

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4567: Deprecate kubernetes-ro service

Issue description:
Now that the "secrets" type has been merged, and we have namespaces, I don't think it often makes sense to give blanket readonly access to objects.  So, lets deprecated it.

I don't know that we want to rip it out all in one go.
Nothing is using the `kubernetes-ro` service as far as I can see from searching the codebase, however some customers might depend on it, and maybe openshift does.  For GKE, I think we'd like it gone.  So, lets add a flag to the master that disables its creation.  If a customer needs it we can tell them how to get it back, but it will discourage new uses.

Once service-accounts land, we can give people that need it a way to automatically generate policy and credentials for things in pods.  Then we can delete `kubernetes-ro` it altogether.

PR title: verify and default APIVersion in createHandler, verify APIVersion in UpdateResource

With this PR,

Issue #10356: Heapster should use a service account for auth

Issue description:
Heapster currently uses a [system secret](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/addons/cluster-monitoring/standalone/heapster-controller.yaml#L46) to authenticate to the apiserver. Heapster should instead use the service account (like we do for DNS) so that it works without any special configuration on all cloud providers.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7257: Document best practices for Kubernetes users

Issue description:
We should document best practices for using Kubernetes, especially within the context of creating new examples (#4926), so that reviewers can check for the issues. This is a successor to #1603.

Off the top of my head:
- Use the latest stable API version (currently v1)
- Use YAML rather than JSON (more user friendly for config)
- Group related objects together in a single file. This currently requires a List object in YAML, but it's still better than separate files. Almost nobody knows about this feature.
- Create service before corresponding replication controllers so that the scheduler can spread the pods comprising the service. #11144 (or, create the RC without specifying replicas, create the service, then scale up the RC, which may work better in an example using progressive disclosure and may have benefits in real scenarios also, such as ensuring one replica works before creating lots of them)
- Use `kubectl create -f <directory>` where possible. Another little-known feature.
- Don't use hostPort unless absolutely necessary (e.g., for a node daemon). Use the apiserver proxying or port forwarding for debug/admin access, or a service for external service access. Though #1487 was closed, hostPort is still in several examples.
- Don't specify default values unnecessarily. Now that we default the selector and labels in RC, it should get slimmer. Eventually we'll need a user's guide that can cover more advanced topics, but we want examples to look simple, in general.
- We should establish a convention other than "name" for label keys. (#3394) Probably some combination of "app", "component", ... I put some examples in labels.md.
- Service should use a subset of the labels used by the replication controllers whose pods it targets. #8524
- Use kubectl run and expose where appropriate, at least presented as an alternative
- Use headless services where appropriate
- Use kubectl bulk operations (via files and/or labels) for get and delete
- Use kubectl delete rather than stop
- No naked pods, except for RestartNever scenarios. (A minimal Job is coming. #1624)
- Use Deployment (#1743) for RestartAlways services rather than RC directly, when we have that.
- In the meantime, put a version number or hash as a suffix to the name and in a label on a ReplicationController, to facilitate rolling update, as we do for [--image](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/072137764665182394975e1e1459ade58ee25719/pkg/kubectl/rolling_updater.go#L112)
- Put object description in an annotation

Issue #11321: Explicit errors while detaching GCE PD prevent PD from ever being detached

Issue description:
If `GetCloudProvider` or `DetachDisk` calls fail while detaching a GCE PD, because the previous `Unmount` call succeeded, there are no further attempts by kubelet to detach the PD, and the PD remains attached to the node indefinitely.

Code in question [pkg/volume/gce_pd/gce_util.go#L114](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/gce_pd/gce_util.go#L114):

```
    // Detach the disk
    gce, err := cloudprovider.GetCloudProvider("gce", nil)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if err := gce.(*gce_cloud.GCECloud).DetachDisk(pd.pdName); err != nil {
        return err
    }
```

`verifyDetached(pd, gce)` is called to ensure retries on silent failures of the detach call (which are much more common); explicit failures should also be handled similarly.

Issue #4366: kubectl run should support run-once commands

Issue description:
When I run the simplest form of `run-container`:

```
$ kubectl run-container vmarmol-secret vmarmol/secret:latest
```

I expected this to be a one-time pod (it is a command I was running to test HTTPS connections and exits quickly). However, in reality it created a replicaController pod. According to the examples in kubectl.sh:

```
    $ kubectl run-container nginx --image=dockerfile/nginx
    // Starts a single instance of nginx.

    $ kubectl run-container nginx --image=dockerfile/nginx --replicas=5
    // Starts a replicated instance of nginx.
```

I was expecting to need to use the `--replicas` flag in order to get that behavior. Is this intended? The implementation currently takes the default of `--replicas=1` which probably explains the behavior.

Issue #12531: Pages corrupted: Titles in front matter with a colon ( : ) are causing Jekyll build errors

Issue description:
Can we wrap all auto-generated front matter titles in quotation marks during pre-publishing processing?

**Issue:**
Colons are causing this build error:

```
(<unknown>): mapping values are not allowed in this context
```

Pages that have build errors do not display correctly out on the site, for example: http://kubernetes.io/v1.0/docs/admin/cluster-components.html
Here is that page's current frontmatter:

```

---
layout: docwithnav
title: Kubernetes Cluster Admin Guide: Cluster Components

---
```

**Proposed Solution:**
If we wrap all titles in quotations, this resolves any errors caused by titles that contain colons and the pages display as expected:

---
layout: docwithnav
title: "Kubernetes Cluster Admin Guide: Cluster Components"

---

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #13920: "Long" inter-node transfers on pod network often hang on Vagrant

Issue description:
I am experiencing frequent hangs on large transfers (> 12 KB)  between nodes when using the pod network;  that is, between 10.246.x.n and 10.246.y.m for x != y.   The larger the transfer the more likely the hang.  I first noticed the problem on http responses of 33 kb, which hang at about the 12 kb mark 50% time and succeed the rest of the time.  Larger transfers hang more frequently but always at about the 12 kb mark. I see the problem with both http and ssh (scp) transfers.  I see the problem for all four combinations of (node,pod) on one node to (node,pod) on another.  I see the problem for master to minion and minion to minion transfers.

I do not see any problem within a single node (10.246.x.n to 10.246.x.m).  I do not see any problem when using the host network (10.245 addresses).

I have tried Kubernetes 1.0.5 using Vagrant 1.7.4 and VirtualBox 5.0.2 on a Mac host, as well as Kubernetes 1.0.6 using Vagrant 1.7.4 and VirtualBox 5.0.4 on a Linux host.  Both show the same problem.  I even tried switching the os for the vagrant nodes from Fedora 21 to 22.  That caused lots of other problems, but this network hanging issue was still there.

I looked at the network traffic using Wireshark.  When the problem occurred, an ICMP redirect message would be sent from the pod ip of the host node (10.246.x.1) to the pod ip of the server (10.246.x.4 in my case) redirecting the stream to the host ip of the destination (10.246.y.1) (which was also the destination).  This was immediately followed by a retransmission of the original packet with the same IP addresses (i.e. from 10.246.x.4 to 10.246.y.1) but with different mac addresses.  Wireshark flagged this second packet as a retransmission.

The same sequence of 3 packets would then repeat periodically (except Wireshark would flag both data packets as retransmissions).

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/13920

Once this lands, I will back port it to 1.0.x release stream.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #15333: [RFC] improve `kubectl annotate` and `kubectl label` to increase success rate

Issue description:
`kubectl label` and `kubectl annotate` work in this pattern: first issuing a "GET" to the API server to retrieve the latest object, then adding the label/annotation to the object, and finally issuing an "PUT" with the modified object. The request will fail if the object stored in the server has been updated between the "GET" and "PUT", even if the update has no conflict with the label/annotate request. In such cases, instead of returning an error, `kubectl` should retry without disturbing the end user.

There are two ways to implement this:
1. retry in kubectl: simply retry the label/annotate process several times if the server rejected the request because the object has been updated. The only exception is when the `--resource-version` [precondition](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubectl/cmd/annotate.go#L52) is set, then kubectl shouldn't retry.
2. use the strategicMergePatch instead of calling Update at client-side. PATCH is more robust because PATCH does the "get, modify, update" in the server-side, so there is less chance to have a conflict, and PATCH will retry at the server-side (see #14758). We need to make some adaptions though:
- kubectl annotate/label has the `--overwrite` [flag](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubectl/cmd/annotate.go#L51), when it's false, kubectl should retrieve the latest object to confirm there is no existing annotation/label of the same key, and then proceed with issuing the patch.
- if the `--resource-version` [flag](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubectl/cmd/annotate.go#L52) is set, ~~we should fall back to the current behavior, because PATCH doesn't support the resource-version precondition.~~ [UPDATE:] we just need to specify the resourVersion in the patch, then it will be treated as a precondition by the UpdateResource() handler in the API server.

I plan to take the first approach as an immediate fix.

Issue #16733: pod quota cpu limit exceeded message is confusing

Issue description:
If you have a project that has a quota and a limitrange:

```
apiVersion: v1
items:
- apiVersion: v1
  kind: ResourceQuota
  metadata:
    creationTimestamp: 2015-11-03T15:42:46Z
    name: sinatra-quota
    namespace: sinatra
    resourceVersion: "2113"
    selfLink: /api/v1/namespaces/sinatra/resourcequotas/sinatra-quota
    uid: 876c921f-8241-11e5-a64b-525400b33d1d
  spec:
    hard:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 512Mi
      pods: "3"
      replicationcontrollers: "3"
      resourcequotas: "1"
      services: "3"
  status:
    hard:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 512Mi
      pods: "3"
      replicationcontrollers: "3"
      resourcequotas: "1"
      services: "3"
    used:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 100Mi
      pods: "1"
      replicationcontrollers: "2"
      resourcequotas: "1"
      services: "1"
- apiVersion: v1
  kind: LimitRange
  metadata:
    creationTimestamp: 2015-11-03T15:42:46Z
    name: sinatra-limits
    namespace: sinatra
    resourceVersion: "1570"
    selfLink: /api/v1/namespaces/sinatra/limitranges/sinatra-limits
    uid: 87a02697-8241-11e5-a64b-525400b33d1d
  spec:
    limits:
    - max:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 750Mi
      min:
        cpu: 10m
        memory: 5Mi
      type: Pod
    - default:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 100Mi
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 100Mi
      max:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 750Mi
      min:
        cpu: 10m
        memory: 5Mi
      type: Container
kind: List
metadata: {}
```

When you try to deploy a new pod, the default (from the limitrange) is inherited by the deployer pod. In this case, 100m cpu.

So, if you already have 2 pods scheduled (using 200m cpu), you are at quota/limit. Then, when the deployer tries to deploy something else, you get this error:

```
Error creating: Pod "ruby-example-2-" is forbidden: unable to admit pod without exceeding quota for resource cpu:  limited to 200m but require 300m to succeed.
```

If you read this error, on the surface it seems to indicate the wrong thing. It talks about "unable to admit pod" and then says "limited to 200m".

The reality is that the **project** is limited to 200m of total CPU, and we're already using that much. Scheduling this pod (whose requirement is 100m) would result in a total scheduled amount of 300m, which is over quota.

Perhaps a different wording could be something like:

```
Error creating: Pod "ruby-example-2-" is forbidden: quota exceeded for resource cpu:  project limited to 200m, current usage is 200m, pod requires 100m
```

Or more generally, the format of:

```
project limit is X, current usage is Y, and you're asking for Z more
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #17285: [1.1.1] heapster RC creation failure due to missing NUM_MINIONS variable in minion user data

Issue description:
Hi, I just started playing with kubernetes v1.1.1 on AWS using the following config:

```
export KUBERNETES_PROVIDER=aws
export KUBE_AWS_ZONE=eu-west-1a
export NUM_MINIONS=1
export MASTER_SIZE=c4.large
export MINION_SIZE=r3.large
export AWS_S3_REGION=eu-west-1
export AWS_S3_BUCKET=xxx
export KUBE_AWS_INSTANCE_PREFIX=xxx
```

Unfortunately the very first thing I encountered was that cluster monitoring addon was broken. Apparently the heapster RC was missing. I found out that the [RC spec for heapster](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/addons/cluster-monitoring/influxdb/heapster-controller.yaml#L2) relies on `num_nodes` salt variable, which gets defined by [cluster/aws/templates/create-dynamic-salt-files.sh](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/aws/templates/create-dynamic-salt-files.sh#L43), which on the other hand is invoked by the [k8s master start (user data) script](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/aws/util.sh#L876). Unfortunately the variable that `create-dynamic-salt-files.sh` relies on (NUM_MINIONS) is not provided to the master start script, hence `num_nodes` gets no value (in fact it evaluates to None, which can be observed later on in salt logs).

I'll provide a patch for this issue but I haven't signed the CLA yet, so feel free to fix this on your own.

BTW, does anyone test Kubernetes on AWS regularly or at least just before a release is made? Is AWS support considered official/stable? I mostly use default configs and this is not the first time I encounter such a fundamental issue.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #18531: Clean up the API initialization process in package registered and package install

Issue description:
Currently, API registration is in done in the [`registered` package](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/registered/registered.go) and the `install` package in each API, e.g., [the `install` package for group ""](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/install/install.go). The `registered` package keeps a hard-coded list of valid GroupVersions and a hard-coded list of GroupVersions that are enabled by default. This is against our goal of separating API machinery from the API.

We plan to remove the `init()` in package `registered` and do all the API initialization in each `install` package. To do so, we conceptually split the API initialization into 2 steps:
The first step is registration, instead of a hard-coded list, each install package adds their group/versions to the `registered.validGroupVersions` list;
The second step is installation, each `install` package calls a function provided by the `registered` package to learn which group/version the user wants to install, as expressed in KUBE_API_VERSIONS, and then install them. If the environment variable is not set, then all registered group/version will be installed.

The `install` package should export the installation function so that an API can be installed after initialization. [edit] The installation function installs the API without checking `KUBE_API_VERSIONS`. I think @nikhiljindal needs this feature for his apiserver library.

cc @nikhiljindal @deads2k

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: cleanup package `registered` and `install`
PR description:
fix #18531

Some highlights of the PR:
1. in package `registered`, I remove the hard-coded list of valid versions and the hard-coded list of versions that are supported by default
2. The `install` package in each group initiate the group installation process. It depends on the `registered` package to check if a version should be enabled and keep records of enabled groups. The `init()` function in the `register` package in each version is changed to an exported function named `Register()`, and `install` will call it to add the version to the `Scheme`.
3. The `import_known_versions.go` in each binary imports the `install` package and calls a function exported by the `registered` package to check if all versions specified in KUBE_API_VERSIONS are installed.
4. [edit] The order of versions in KUBE_API_VERSIONS is not significant anymore. The preference of versions is specified in `availableVersions` in each `install` package (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/install/install.go#L42).

~~Note this PR doesn't implement exactly what I wrote in #18531. Specifically this PR doesn't distinguish `registered versions` from `enabled versions`, because I find it's useless to have versions that are registered but not enabled.~~

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #19405: BufferQueueLimitError in the fluentd container of the master

Issue description:
I have a cluster in GCE. `Major:"1", Minor:"2+", GitVersion:"v1.2.0-alpha.3"`. I have enabled logging to GCP. Updated from a previous 1.1 version in November.

Yesterday the fluentd container of the master started emitting these errors twice per second approximately:

```
[warn]: emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error="queue size exceeds limit" tag="fluent.warn"
[warn]: emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error="queue size exceeds limit" tag="fluent.warn"
[warn]: emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error="queue size exceeds limit" tag="kubelet"
[warn]: suppressed same stacktrace
```

It kept that way until I manually restarted the Docker container today. It didn't send any logs to the console in the meantime.

Some logged errors had more details:

```
[error]: failed to emit fluentd's log event tag="fluent.warn" event={"error_class"=>"Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError", "error"=>"queue size exceeds limit", "tag"=>"kubelet", "message"=>"emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error=\"queue size exceeds limit\" tag=\"kubelet\""} error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error=#<Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError: queue size exceeds limit>
```

Tags are always `kubelet`, `kube-apiserver` or `fluent.warn` in all errors I have seen.

There were some `Faraday::Timeout` and `Faraday::SSLError` some hours before, but no other sign of malfunction. I have the minions fluentd pods in a permanent `Terminating` status which expired in November, but the containers are still alive and working and I think it has been solved in this other issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17929

If the real cause of this error can't be found at least the fluentd container of the master should be prepared to restart itself if it cannot work correctly anymore.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Update to the latest version of google-fluentd.
PR description:
It includes some performance improvements for parsing JSON (which is
very important for us, since all Docker logs are JSON) as well as a
couple new settings, like forcing of a flush of multiline logs after a
time period rather than having to wait until a new log is seen before
feeling confident flushing the previous one.

It also adds the `buffer_queue_full_action` option, but I'm not as confident about how stable that is, so I've opened #22537 to track it.

cc @jimmidyson in case we're able to similarly get an updated version of fluentd for fluentd-es. I unfortunately am pretty swamped with other things at the moment.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #23278: Introducing protobuf tags changes behavior api.ObjectMetaFor

Issue description:
After running protobuf generator some unit tests are not passing, e.g.: TestAnnotateObjectFromFile

I did some debugging and the issue is basically, that (at least in this particula case):
  api.ObjectMetaFor(&v1.Pod{})
returns:
  unexpected error: couldn't assign/convert *v1.ObjectMeta to *api.ObjectMeta

The reason for that is that:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/runtime/helper.go#L52

underlying is calling:
ConvertibleTo:
https://github.com/golang/go/blob/f2772a49353e09e4e00121ca4e538a3b3302a1de/src/reflect/type.go#L97

And the issue is that ConvertibleTo requires tags for all fields to be exactly the same:
https://github.com/golang/go/blob/f2772a49353e09e4e00121ca4e538a3b3302a1de/src/reflect/type.go#L1410

So we:
- either need to generate tags also for internal types
- review all usecases of ConvertibleTo in our code and change it to our custom code

I think the first one is much better.

@smarterclayton - thoughs?

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #24352: Resource quota should ignore pod resource requirement updates

Issue description:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/quota/evaluator/core/pods.go#L50

The scenario that presented a problem was the following:

a) create pods in a namespace that do not make a memory claim
b) add a quota that tracks memory
c) update one of the pods previously created by reducing its active deadline.

Expected result:
Since a pod cannot change its resources via update, we should have been allowed to update the pod spec.

Actual Result:
error since the pod did not make a memory claim, quota rejects the pod.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Quota ignores pod compute resources on updates
PR description:
Scenario:
1. define a quota Q that tracks memory and cpu
2. create pod P that uses memory=100Mi, cpu=100m

Issue #24089: kubectl validation fails when creating a non-v1 object in a v1 list

Issue description:
In other words, you can't create/replace/delete/apply deployments with kubectl if they're in a list.

Works as expected:

``` console
$ cat nginx-rc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: List
items:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: ReplicationController
    metadata:
      name: nginx
    spec:
      replicas: 1
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            name: nginx
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: nginx
              image: nginx
$ kubectl create -f nginx-rc.yaml
replicationcontroller "nginx" created
```

Does not work as expected:

```
$ cat nginx-dpl.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: List
items:
  - apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
    kind: Deployment
    metadata:
      name: nginx
    spec:
      replicas: 1
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            name: nginx
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: nginx
              image: nginx
$ kubectl create -f nginx-dpl.yaml
error validating "nginx-dpl.yaml": error validating data: couldn't find type: v1beta1.Deployment; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false
$ kubectl create -f nginx-dpl.yaml --validate=false
deployment "nginx" created
```

This is a high priority issue for us, since it means we can't (easily) use apply (or any kubectl command) with lists of JSON objects since we've moved all our replication controllers over to deployment objects, which is hampering the UX of our config efforts.

Issue #25484: Weird quota and limitrange behavior

Issue description:
I'm using HEAD in the master branch with a simple 1 master + 1 slave setup. API server is started with the following flag: `--admission-control=LimitRanger,NamespaceLifecycle,ResourceQuota`.

To reproduce:

```
kubectl create namespace test
kubectl --namespace=test create -f docs/admin/resourcequota/quota.yaml
kubectl --namespace=test create -f docs/admin/limitrange/limits.yaml
kubectl --namespace=test run nginx --image=nginx:latest --requests="cpu=500m,mem=100mi"
```

Of course, no pods will be created because "cpu=500m" exceeds the default value of "cpu=300m". This is expected behavior. However, the unexpected part is when I do a `kubectl describe namespace test`, and the cpu usage was showing:

```
Resource Quotas
 Name:          quota
 Resource       Used    Hard
 --------       --- ---
 cpu            1500m   20
 memory         300Mi   1Gi
```

As each container was supposed to request 500m cpu, this looks like replicaset controller is trying to create more pods after previous ones were rejected, and this causes the quota usage to keep increasing. This will continue until the quota controller runs and reconciliates the actual information (by default it runs every 5 minutes). I'm wondering if this is the intended behavior, as this could cause all the quota to be used up very quickly until the quota controller runs the next time, and effectively, this blocks all the future pod creation.

PR title: use monotonic now in TestDelNode
PR description:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/24971.

Briefly, the rate_limited_queue uses a `container/heap` to store values, and use this data structure to ensure we can always fetch the value with the minimum `processAt`. However, in some extreme condition, the continuous call to `time.Now()` would get the same value, which causes some unpredictable order in the queue, this fix uses a monotonic `now()` to avoid that.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #27062: Downward API for resource specification should default to node capacity when limits are not set.

Issue description:
As of now the downward API for resource specification defaults to `0` for `limits` when `limits` are not specified in the pod spec. This behavior is not ideal for applications.
What does a limit of `0` mean?
In reality, not having a limit translates to being limited by node capacity as of now, and node allocatable in the future once it is enforced.
We should default to node capacity instead of setting `limit.memory` to `0` when `limits` are not set.
And for `limits.cpu` we should again default to node capacity and allocatable in the future.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #27378: nsenter mount gets doesn't list the right mounts, causing containerized kubelet unable to detach cloud disk

Issue description:
In nsenter_mounter, [List()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/util/mount/nsenter_mount.go#L161) reads mounts from `/rootfs/proc/mounts`. Because `/proc/mounts` is sym link to `/proc/self/mounts` and the containerized kubelet usually bind mount host rootfs in slave mode, thus containerized kubelet's mounts is different from what host sees.

This causes kubelet unable to umount/detach volumes.

The right way to do is to read hosts's proc, i.e. `/rootfs/proc/1/mounts`

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #27582: node e2e test teardown crashes with nil deref if node services could not be started

Issue description:
In `/test/e2e_node/e2e_node_suite_test.go`, the node services are started in the `BeforeSuite` logic. If they fail to start, ginkgo's `Fail` function is called, which ultimately initiates test tear down and thus the `AfterSuite` logic in the same file.

The `AfterSuite` logic calls `e2es.stop()` (defined in `test/e2e_node/e2e_service.go`), which will try to e.g. `es.stopService(es.kubeletCmd)`, where `es` is the `e2eService` and `kubeletCmd` is the `*killCmd` for the kubelet service.

Unfortunately, because the service failed to start, this pointer is nil, and we get a nil pointer dereference in the `Kill` function (in `test/e2e_node/e2e_service.go`).

Off the top of my head, I see two potential solutions to this problem.
1. Pre-allocate default `killCmd` structs on the `e2eService` struct created in the `newE2eService` function in `test/e2e_node/e2e_service.go`. We could just make `killCmd.cmd = nil` on these, because the assumption appears to be that if `killCmd.cmd == nil`, the service is not running. (It appears that prior to the addition of `killCmd`, a nil `cmd` was interpreted as 'service not running,' and that this `cmd` field got rolled into `killCmd`, see 66d74f969dbbde894949b87366d215e020167faf).
2. Or, simply add an additional check to the `Kill` function, where we assume that if the `killCmd` is `nil`, the respective service is not running.

Thoughts? I want to make sure I'm not missing something here.

@timstclair because you added teardown code in 66d74f969dbbde894949b87366d215e020167faf
@euank because you added `killCmd` in 34996f1b84104a83033fb62cec72ec86f9eef8c1

Issue #26183: OS_DISTRIBUTION should be split into two vars

Issue description:
This came up while I was working on #25977, for which I am adding support to run clusters with the master on GCI and nodes on Debian. I find it difficult to do within current framework that uses a single env var, `OS_DISTRIBUTION`, to select the OS distro for both the master and nodes. Issue #28515: kube-dns v15+ cannot set verbosity

Issue description:
When replacing kube-dns v11 (as defined w/ the v1.2.4 release) with v15 in the v1.3.0 release, we notice that the `skydns` container inside the `kube-dns` pod is overly verbose. This appears to be due to an inability to turn of `Info` logging within [dns.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/dns/dns.go#L583). A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #29358: GCE PD Detach fails if node no longer exists Issue description: **Problem:** If a node with a GCE PD attached is deleted (before the volume is detached), subsequent attempts by the attach/detach controller to detach it continuously fail, and prevent the controller from attaching the volume to another node. **Repro steps:** 1. Create a pod referencing a GCE PD 2. Wait for pod to get scheduled and running. 3. Delete the node VM (using gcloud) that the pod is scheduled to. 4. Check if volume is detached by attach/detach controller: - _Expected:_ Volume detached. - _Actual:_ Volume continuously fails detach. **Logs:**
From `/var/log/kube-controller-manager.log`: ``` I0721 03:21:43.464087 7 reconciler.go:134] Started DetachVolume for volume "X" from node "Y" due to maxWaitForUnmountDuration expiry. E0721 03:21:43.591941 7 gce.go:2580] getInstanceByName/single-zone: failed to get instance Y; err: googleapi: Error 404: The resource 'projects/[project]/zones/[zone]/instances/Y' was not found, notFound E0721 03:21:43.591985 7 attacher.go:215] Error checking if PD ("[pdname]") is already attached to current node ("Y"). messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #30792: Add Encryption to dynamic provisioner Issue description: ## Summary Encrypted volumes is a commonly requested feature for Kubernetes storage and requirements exist downstream to use encrypted volumes. The following is a summary of the three cloud providers that allow dynamic provisioning and the current state of volume encryption for each. **_TL;DR:_**  Add encryption support for EBS PersistentVolumes. AWS has optional encryption and allows key via the API. GCE encrypts volumes by default but does not allow user-defined keys in the API. GCE allows custom keys via manual volume creation in the UI.  Cinder volumes can be manually created w/ encryption. @kubernetes/sig-storage @abhgupta @thockin @saad-ali I'm going to follow up with a PR today/tomorrow to meet the 1.4 cutoff on Friday. ## Encryption by Cloud Provider ### AWS - AWS does _not_ encrypt volumes by default - AWS API allows an optional boolean flag for encryption - AWS API allows a user to specify which key to use for encryption with a default key provided by AWS if not specified. See: - [http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AmazonEBS.html](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/AmazonEBS.html) - [http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/EBSEncryption.html) - [http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateVolume.html](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateVolume.html) ### GCE - GCE encrypts all volumes by default - Users can provide their own keys, but this is a manual step in the UI only. - GCE API does _not_ provide a way to specify which key should encrypt which disk - Volume attachment to the node requires the same key it is encrypted with. This is a manual step in the UI only. See: - [https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-supplied-encryption](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/customer-supplied-encryption) - [https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/latest/disks/insert](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/latest/disks/insert) ### Cinder - No encryption by default - No opt-in encryption via API - Block storage can be optionally encrypted - Manual creation of the volumes is required See: - [https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/VolumeEncryption](https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/VolumeEncryption) - [http://docs.openstack.org/mitaka/config-reference/block-storage/volume-encryption.html](http://docs.openstack.org/mitaka/config-reference/block-storage/volume-encryption.html) - [http://docs.openstack.org/juno/config-reference/content/section_create-encrypted-volume-type.html](http://docs.openstack.org/juno/config-reference/content/section_create-encrypted-volume-type.html) ## Proposed Workflow: 1. Admins create however many keys in AWS as they wish. This is a manual step. 2. Admins create StorageClasses with the fully-qualified AWS resource name for the key. Implementation details: - Add encryption support to AWS cloud provider - Add encryption support to Kubernetes EBS volume plugin - Use StorageClass for both the Encrypted boolean and EncryptionKeyName in PV controller A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Add encryption to EBS dynamic provisioner PR description: Resolves https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/30792 Adds encryption to the EBS cloud provider and provisioner. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #31765: Node E2E: stop-services option not working properly. Issue description: In node e2e, we have the `stop-services` option to keep the services running after test for further debug. However, we set `Pdeathsig` to `SIGTERM` for the services, which means that once the parent exits, they will receive `SIGTERM` and exit with the parent if they don't trap the signal. With this, `stop-services` option will never work. If we still need this feature, we should not set `Pdeathsig` if `stop-services` is false. @vishh /cc @kubernetes/sig-node A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Node E2E: Cleanup e2e services PR description: fixes #31765. This PR is composed of 2 commits: - The 1st commit split services.go into: `services.go`, `server.go` and `internal_services.go`: - `services.go` contains the public object `E2EServices` which is used by the test framework directly. - `internal_services.go` contains the internal object `e2eServices` which manages internal (statically-linked) services - apiserver, etcd and namespace_controller. - `server.go` is the object managing exec process, both internal_services and kubelet are running as separate processes and managed with server.go. - The 2nd commit added `monitorParent` option in start function of `E2EServices`. messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #29155: E2E & Node E2E: Add image white list Issue description: For https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/29081. With https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/28807, we are going to share some tests between e2e and node e2e. However, one problem is that e2e and node e2e have different image prepulling. When adding a test which needs an new image, it's pain to add the image in both of them. And both of them are hard to maintain. Mostly, people just didn't realize they've introduced an new image, and even though, the test can still pass in most cases. This causes issues like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28868. To avoid this, we should add an image white list. Only images in the white list could be used in the test. Because all pods should be created via [`CreatePod`](https://github.com/Random-Liu/kubernetes/blob/e40e82bd5c724675c26ca03a631171ecf6305cac/test/e2e/framework/pods.go#L46) in the future, we can do some check in it to make sure all images are in the whitelist. If we can make sure that all images are successfully pulled before test, we can even set the `ImagePullPolicy` to `Never` for all pods. This could be easily achieved in node e2e test framework, because we already have a similar white list in the test infrastructure. However, for regular e2e, the image list is hard coded in the [spec of static pod `e2e-image-puller`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/saltbase/salt/e2e-image-puller/e2e-image-puller.manifest#L30). To achieve this, we need to change it to a `DaemonSet` and do some other walkaround. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/26110 @yujuhong /cc @kubernetes/sig-node A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: Node E2E: Add image white list PR description: This is part of #29081. Fixes #29155. As is discussed with @yujuhong in #29155, it is difficult to maintain the prepull image list if it is not enforced. This PR added an image white list in the test framework, only images in the white list could be used in the test. A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #33625: Esipp transition plan

Issue description:
Alpha to beta (1.5):
- Declare 2 sets of annotations, one in the alpha namespace (already exists) and one in the beta namespace (new)
- alpha always takes precedence
- If alpha is set to a valid value, we write the beta annotation to mirror it clobbering any user field

Why convert alpha to beta:
1. Users are auto transitioned
2. Not converting means if alpha and beta are set to 2 different values, deleting the alpha requires a cleanup of the alpha value, and an activation of the beta value. This might be confusing and error prone.
3. Not converting makes handling updates harder, as we would have to allow updates to the "inactive" one.

Beta to GA (1.6):
- Declare 2 fields that mirros the annotations in beta
- Ignore alpha annotations (any alpha annotations in play will continue to work because they were translated to the beta annotation)
- Perform the same conversion time clobbering

If users upgrade from 1.4 to 1.6 directly, the alpha annotation is ignored and esipp stops working.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Promotes Source IP preservation for Virtual IPs from Beta to GA
PR description:
Fixes #33625. Feature issue: kubernetes/features#27.

Bullet points:
- Declare 2 fields (ExternalTraffic and HealthCheckNodePort) that mirror the ESIPP annotations.

- Allow promoting beta annotations to first class fields or reversely.
- Disallow setting invalid ExternalTraffic and HealthCheckNodePort on services. Default ExternalTraffic field for nodePort or loadBalancer type service to "Global" if not set.

Issue #42929: pkg/util/flock.Acquire() doesn't guarantee mutual exclusion

Issue description:
**BUG REPORT**:

**Kubernetes version latest master**:

**Environment**:
- **Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Linux 4.2.0-42-generic**:

**What happened**:
The `flock.Acquire()` doesn't provide mutual exclusion. Two processes can both grab the same flock at the same time.

**What you expected to happen**:
Only one process should be able to grab the flock.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```shell
cat testflock.go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/util/flock"
)

func main() {
	if err := flock.Acquire("/tmp/foo.lock"); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("error:", err)
		return
	}

	fmt.Println("acquired")

	time.Sleep(time.Hour)
}

go build testflock.go; ./testflock
acquired

# open another terminal and run
./testflock
acquired
```

**Anything else we need to know**:

Although the flock doesn't work, the [watchForLockfileContention()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.0/cmd/kubelet/app/server.go#L324) does work. Since we _usually_ specify `--exit-on-lock-contention` together with `--lock-file`, so the 1st process will exit anyway.
However we still need to fix the flock..

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: pkg/util/flock: Fix the flock so it actually locks.

With this PR, the second call to `Acquire()` will block unless the lock is released (process exits).
Also removed the memory mutex in the previous code since we don't need `Release()` here so no need to save and protect the local fd.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #43459: CVE-2017-1000056: PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin authorizes incorrectly

Issue description:
A PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin vulnerability allows users to make use of any PodSecurityPolicy object, even ones they are not authorized to use.

CVE: CVE-2017-1000056

* Fixed in [v1.5.5](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases/tag/v1.5.5) in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/7fef0a4f6a44ea36f166c39fdade5324eff2dd5e
* Fixed in release-1.5 branch in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/43491
* Fixed in master in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/43489

**Who is affected?**
Only Kubernetes 1.5.0-1.5.4 installations that do _all_ of the following:
* Enable the PodSecurityPolicy API (which is not enabled by default):
      `--runtime-config=extensions/v1beta1/podsecuritypolicy=true`
* Enable the PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin (which is not enabled by default):
      `--admission-control=...,PodSecurityPolicy,...`
* Use authorization to limit users' ability to use specific PodSecurityPolicy objects

kubeadm and GKE do not allow enabling PodSecurityPolicy in 1.5, so are not affected by this vulnerability.

kube-up.sh and kops do not enable PodSecurityPolicy by default, so are not affected by this vulnerability. A modified kube-up.sh or kops deployment could have enabled it.

**What is the impact?**
A user that is authorized to create pods can make use of any existing PodSecurityPolicy, even ones they are not authorized to use.

**How can I mitigate this prior to installing 1.5.5?**
1. Export existing PodSecurityPolicy objects:
      `kubectl get podsecuritypolicies -o yaml > psp.yaml`

2. Review and delete any PodSecurityPolicy objects you do not want all pod-creating users to be able to use (NOTE: Privileged users that were making use of those policies will also lose access to those policies). For example:
      `kubectl delete podsecuritypolicies/my-privileged-policy`

3. After upgrading to 1.5.5, re-create the exported PodSecurityPolicy objects:
      `kubectl create -f psp.yaml`

PR title: Include system:authenticated group when impersonating
PR description:
Fixes #43227

An authorized impersonation request solely for a specific username previously resulted in a `user.Info` that did not include either the `system:authenticated` or `system:unauthenticated` groups. That meant that permissions intended to be granted to all users, like discovery, would be denied the impersonated user.

This allows `kubectl get pods --as=<username>` to work as expected

```release-note

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #43662: In-cluster config for kubectl cannot be disabled/overriden

Issue description:
I have an app running in a pod that shells out to kubectl. A kubeconfig file with credentials for four different clusters is included in the pod. However, kubectl always detects that it's being run from inside a cluster and uses the pod's cluster's apiserver instead of the credentials I'm explicitly passing it. I've tried various things to disable this detection and make it use the configuration I'm supplying, but it always uses the in-cluster configuration settings, which results in not only submitting to the wrong cluster, but this error being returned for many resources being applied:

```
the namespace from the provided object "foo" does not match the namespace "bar". You must pass '--namespace=foo' to perform this operation.
```

where "foo" refers to the resource I'm trying to create with `kubectl apply` (the namespace of the resource is in the input file) and "bar" is the namespace of the pod shelling out to kubectl. Running the exact same command locally works, because kubectl is not overriding what I pass it with in-cluster configuration.

Specifically, the command being run is:

```
kubectl --kubeconfig /path/to/.kube/config --context my-context apply -f resources.yml
```

I can't find any documentation on how to disable in-cluster config. I looked through the code of the Go client to try to figure out how it's choosing to do this. I tried various things to disable it, including:

* Setting the `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` environment variable to an empty string, due to this: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/49948ae0ca8eb31d632fbf346e25ee0eb6762d5b/tools/clientcmd/client_config.go#L505. But Kubernetes overrides my setting and fills in the environment variable like normal.
* Mounting an empty volume to /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount to try to prevent Kubernetes from mounting the service account files, but it mounts them anyway, overriding my explicit mount.
* Setting the `KUBECONFIG` environment variable to the path of the file I want it to use. It has no effect.

This is kubectl 1.5.x running in a Kubernetes 1.5 cluster. Notably, using kubectl 1.4.x does _not_ exhibit this behavior in the same Kubernetes 1.5 cluster. kubectl 1.4 works as expected.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Explicit namespace from kubeconfig should override in-cluster config
PR description:
Fixes #43662

If an explicitly specified namespace is read from a kubeconfig file, we should not fall back to in-cluster config

```release-note
kubectl commands run inside a pod using a kubeconfig file now use the namespace specified in the kubeconfig file, instead of using the pod namespace. If no kubeconfig file is used, or the kubeconfig does not specify a namespace, the pod namespace is still used as a fallback.
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #42284: PodDisruptionBudget should use ControllerRef

Issue description:
Currently, PDB uses selector-based listers to determine which controller is managing a given Pod. Now that [ControllerRef](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/controller-ref.md) is implemented across all controllers that PDB looks at, the disruption controller should instead use the ControllerRef on a Pod (if any) to determine which controller manages the Pod.

Without this, PDB may look at the wrong controller(s), thus making the wrong decision about whether to allow an eviction. In the future, this may also allow PDB to respect ownership of Pods by controller types it doesn't know about (third-party controllers), as long as it can access the controller's `/scale` subresource.

@krmayankk I'm assigning to you since you expressed interest in working on this for 1.7. If that's changed, let me know and I'll unassign.

cc @kubernetes/sig-apps-bugs

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #24720: Total priority can overflow

Issue description:
Weight is an int (see [PriorityConfigFactory definition](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae5ac482861382e18b1e7b2943b1b7f333c6a2a/plugin/pkg/scheduler/factory/plugins.go#L53)). Priority can take the range 1-10. Total priority for a node is sum of weight \* priority for each priority function, and the sum is accumulated into an int (see [PrioritizeNodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae5ac482861382e18b1e7b2943b1b7f333c6a2a/plugin/pkg/scheduler/generic_scheduler.go#L227)). So obviously the total priority can overflow if someone sets the weight(s) too high.

The weights of all priority functions are compiled in (or specified in config file), so we can check to make sure maximum total priority can't overflow an int (take sum over all priority functions of 10 \* weight of that priority function, and make sure that's smaller than int(MaxUint >> 1) which according to StackOverflow is the way to find out what is max int (math package has max Int32, Int64, etc. but not max Int).

Note that scheduler extender is OK because although the policy runs in a separate process, the weight is specified in scheduler config file (ExtenderConfig struct) and the priority is bounded 1-10 as usual.

I1029 19:24:24.506359       1 dns.go:240] Have recordset <(clouddns) "buttonmasher-frontend.default.hybrid-cloud-rocks.svc.us-central1-b.us-central1.hybrid-cloud-rocks.com." type=CNAME rrdatas=["buttonmasher-frontend.default.hybrid-cloud-rocks.svc.us-central1.hybrid-cloud-rocks.com."] ttl=180>. After creating the clusters w/ only one zone, the DNS provider worked properly.

**What you expected to happen**:
Cloud DNS Provider should update the DNS record properly w/ multi-zone clusters.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
1. Provision 3 x multi-zone clusters
2. Provision Federation API Server and Controller
3. Add clusters in to federation
4. Deploy federated service and backends

**Anything else do we need to know**:
Using GKE and Cloud DNS

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: deduplicate endpoints before DNS registration
PR description:
**What this PR does / why we need it**: Multizone clusters will return duplicated endpoints to the federation controller manager. The FCM will then attempt to create an A record with duplicate entries, which will fail. As a result, federated services on multi-AZ clusters don't work right now. This PR deduplicates the endpoint IPs before attempting the DNS record registration.

**Which issue this PR fixes**: fixes #35997

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
I believe there is a lot of refactoring required with multizone federated clusters, most notably with regard to AWS and optimising for ALIAS records rather than A, but this PR will at least allow basic functionality to work.

To proxy only part of the kubernetes api and also some static files:

  $ kubectl proxy --www=/my/files --www-prefix=/static/ --api-prefix=/api/

The above lets you 'curl localhost:8001/api/v1/pods'.

To proxy the entire kubernetes api at a different root, use:

  $ kubectl proxy --api-prefix=/custom/

The above lets you 'curl localhost:8001/custom/api/v1/pods'

Examples:
  # Run a proxy to kubernetes apiserver on port 8011, serving static content from ./local/www/
  kubectl proxy --port=8011 --www=./local/www/

  # Run a proxy to kubernetes apiserver on an arbitrary local port.
  # The chosen port for the server will be output to stdout.
  kubectl proxy --port=0

  # Run a proxy to kubernetes apiserver, changing the api prefix to k8s-api
  # This makes e.g. the pods api available at localhost:8001/k8s-api/v1/pods/
  kubectl proxy --api-prefix=/k8s-api

      --reject-paths='^/api/.*/pods/.*/exec,^/api/.*/pods/.*/attach': Regular expression for paths that the proxy should reject.
  -u, --unix-socket='': Unix socket on which to run the proxy.
  -w, --www='': Also serve static files from the given directory under the specified prefix.
  -P, --www-prefix='/static/': Prefix to serve static files under, if static file directory is specified.

Usage:

Issue #47020: Projected volume plugin does not block on data fetch error

Issue description:
When collecting data for a projected volume, if an error is encountered, the plugin logs, but then continues setting up the volume and returns as if it were successful:

```
E0604 10:31:19.324314    3580 projected.go:265] Couldn't get configMap e2e-tests-projected-mnbzg/projected-configmap-test-volume-f1dfa503-4910-11e7-8d9d-0242ac110002: User "system:node:e2e-34198-minion-group-qnk2" cannot get configmaps in the namespace "e2e-tests-proj│
E0604 10:31:19.324409    3580 projected.go:197] Error preparing data for projected volume projected-configmap-volume for pod e2e-tests-projected-mnbzg/pod-projected-configmaps-f1f51bf8-4910-11e7-8d9d-0242ac110002: User "system:node:e2e-34198-minion-group-qnk2" cannot │
I0604 10:31:19.324620    3580 atomic_writer.go:142] pod e2e-tests-projected-mnbzg/pod-projected-configmaps-f1f51bf8-4910-11e7-8d9d-0242ac110002 volume projected-configmap-volume: no update required for target directory /var/lib/kubelet/pods/f2278654-4910-11e7-9d2f-420│
I0604 10:31:19.324667    3580 operation_generator.go:472] MountVolume.SetUp succeeded for volume "projected-configmap-volume" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/projected/f2278654-4910-11e7-9d2f-42010a800002-projected-configmap-volume") pod "pod-projected-configmaps-f1f51bf8│
```

This is because the error returned from collectData() does not short-circuit the SetUp function:
```go
	data, err := s.collectData()
	if err != nil {

	}
```

This means that a pod can start before the configmaps/secrets intended to populate its projected volume exist.

**Kubernetes version** (use `kubectl version`): 1.4.8 (pretty sure problem exists in master)


**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: AWS
- **OS** (e.g. from /etc/os-release): CoreOS 1353.7.0
- **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.9.24
- **Install tools**: Custom AMI


**What happened**:
The service controller deletes and re-adds the ELB listeners when it starts up (or becomes the master).

**What you expected to happen**:
It should only modify the listeners if they have actually changed.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
- Create a service with type `LoadBalancer`
- Restart controller-manager after ELB has been created
- Search CloudTrail for events for the ELB, and verify there are DeleteLoadBalancerListeners and CreateLoadBalancerListeners events.

**Anything else we need to know**:

I believe this is caused by [this for loop](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc568f6433f2d90b30ca8e1d51f3597d60affb11/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L192-L209) in the `ensureLoadBalancer` function which compares the desired listener properties to the actual listener properties.

The problem is that K8 uses lowercase strings [1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc568f6433f2d90b30ca8e1d51f3597d60affb11/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws.go#L2554), [2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc568f6433f2d90b30ca8e1d51f3597d60affb11/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws_test.go#L1149) for the protocols, but AWS returns uppercase protocols when describing the listeners (see the two example outputs below).

I believe the simplest fix is to lowercase the protocols in the for loop when performing the comparison, which I can submit as a PR if others agree with that solution.

From AWS CLI:
```
$ aws elb describe-load-balancers --load-balancer-names a4fafa3e6f24911e6aac506402a2bc46
{
    "LoadBalancerDescriptions": [
         {
             "ListenerDescriptions": [
                {
                    "Listener": {
                        "InstancePort": 32706,
                        "LoadBalancerPort": 80,
                        "Protocol": "TCP",
                        "InstanceProtocol": "TCP"
                    },
                    "PolicyNames": []
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

From Go `elb.DescribeLoadBalancers(request)`
```
package main

import (
	"log"

	"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/aws/session"
	"github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/elb"
)

func main() {
	name := "a4fafa3e6f24911e6aac506402a2bc46"

	sess := session.Must(session.NewSession())
	svc := elb.New(sess)

	request := &elb.DescribeLoadBalancersInput{}
	request.LoadBalancerNames = []*string{&name}

	response, err := svc.DescribeLoadBalancers(request)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	for _, loadBalancer := range response.LoadBalancerDescriptions {
		log.Printf("ELB: %v\n", loadBalancer)
		return
	}
}
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #47092: [GCE] Shared backend services for ILBs leak settings to other ILBs

Issue description:
PR #46663 GCP internal load balancers for services with type LoadBalancer and an annotation specifying "internal".  If the load balancer has `externalTrafficPolicy=Global`, we generate a backend service name such as `k8s-{clusterid}-internal-[tcp/udp]-[clientip|noaffinity]`. This allows other ILBs to utilize the same backend service to keep stay below quota.

However, there are more service settings like `TimeoutSec` and `IAP` which could be unique to a single or multiple load balancers. We need to support users changing these settings (which may require modifying the backend service name format) prior to 1.7 release.  Once the release occurs, it'll be immensely difficult to change names.
