A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #75837: [Kubernetes 1.14.0] Watch on aggregated API resource hangs until first event

Issue description:
**What happened**:

Prior to 1.14, when you created a watch on a resource coming from an aggregated API, you would instantly obtain the `watch.Interface` object, and could stop it when you want.

Since 1.14, when you do the same, the `request.Watch()` method returns when the server sends its first event. Resources directly hosted by the central API-server (core resources, crds, etc.) are not touched by this issue.

When you use higher level APIs like informers, situations like this can make your code hang, as attempts to stop the informer seem ignored (the informer cancellation logic only works once the underlying watch.Interface has been retrieved), and your code hang.

This is hitting https://github.com/docker/cli, and a workaround has been found here: https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/1784. However this change of behavior means that current versions of the CLI can hang when deploying Kubernetes workloads.

**What you expected to happen**:

As with resources hosted by the central API server, the watch.Interface object should be instantly returned

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I'll try to setup an automated test case for that with compose-on-kubernetes.
In the mean-time:
- deploy a kube 1.14 cluster with kind / minikube / ...
- deploy compose-on-kubernetes on it (see https://github.com/docker/compose-on-kubernetes/blob/master/docs/install-on-minikube.md)
- download the latest official docker cli release and try to deploy a simple compose file to kubernetes using `docker stack deploy -c compose-file.yml my-stack --orchestrator=kubernetes`

**Anything else we need to know?**:

After digging a little with a debugging http proxy, I saw that the big difference seem to be that:
- prior to 1.14, when such a watch is issued, the response headers are immediately sent to the client
- with 1.14, on central-API resources, it does not change
- with 1.14, on aggregated API resources, the reponse headers are sent with the first event

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"13", GitVersion:"v1.13.0", GitCommit:"ddf47ac13c1a9483ea035a79cd7c10005ff21a6d", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2018-12-03T21:04:45Z", GoVersion:"go1.11.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"windows/amd64"}

```

Using Kind, also happen with internal Docker Desktop builds

Both Kind, and Linuxkit

Issue #76042: Namespace storage does not remove OrphanFinalizer during cascade deletion

Issue description:
**What happened**:

I created a namespace `foo` with `orphan` finalizer, and then tried to delete it:

```console
$ cat ns.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: foo
  finalizers:
  - orphan
$ kubectl create -f ns.yaml
namespace/foo edited
$ kubectl delete ns foo
namespace "foo" deleted
```

The namespace can be deleted, and the `orphan` finalizer is removed by garbage collection controller:

...
I0401 19:09:56.510632   77981 graph_builder.go:578] GraphBuilder process object: v1/Namespace, namespace , name foo, uid c396b742-9be5-4d5b-b86a-4614853e9516, event type update

Since kubectl species `propagationPolicy: Background`, it is not an orphaning operation, the finalizer should be removed in namespace store.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #76340: Fix concurrent map read and map write in Portworx driver

Issue description:
**What happened**: The Portworx volume driver is accessing the storage parameters and also modifying it. This is a shared map object used by all PVCs being created at that time from the same StorageClass.

This causes 2 issues:

1. The Portworx driver ends up saving annotations of one PVC into the parameters of another PVC as both CreateVolume calls use the same map. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/portworx/portworx_util.go#L76
2. The controller manager crashes as 2 CreateVolume routines try to modify the same map. This is a big problem since the controller manager container crashes half way into creating a volume resulting in the volume being present in the backend portworx cluster but not bound in Kubernetes.

**What you expected to happen**: CreateVolume call for one PVC should be completely isolated from another PVC

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**: Create a large number of PVCs using the Portworx volume driver using the same StorageClass.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #76219: Server-side apply protobuf serialization performance issue

Issue description:
Context
======
 Kubernetes 1.14, ServerSideApply feature enabled on kube-apiserver.

Introduction
=========

Server-Side Apply (SSA) seems to be triggering a performance issue on protobuf serialization of objects, specifically while serializing the new `managedFields` recursive map. We detected the problem because the scalability tests mostly indicated problems in LISTing objects (pods and nodes), even though SSA shouldn't impact this code path.

At this point the problems are probably related to the size of the objects (increased significantly by the additional field) which would lead to:
- more serialization/deserialization,
- more data transfer between client and apiserver,
- more data transfer between apiserver and etcd

Probably many other things, let's try to reproduce.

Steps to reproduce
===============
I'm now comparing the following to set-up:

```bash
# Running without the feature enabled
STORAGE_MEDIA_TYPE=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf \
FEATURE_GATES=ServerSideApply=false \
PATH=$PWD/third_party/etcd:$PATH \
hack/local-up-cluster.sh -O

# Running with the feature enabled
STORAGE_MEDIA_TYPE=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf \
FEATURE_GATES=ServerSideApply=true \
PATH=$PWD/third_party/etcd:$PATH \
hack/local-up-cluster.sh -O
```

I first create a random deployment with a 1000 replicas, the pods don't have to actually start, but should be successfully created.

My benchmark is to run the following python3 script:
```python
import urllib.request
import time
import statistics

request = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/pods",
    headers={
        "Accept": "application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf",
    }
)

size = []
duration = []
NUM_RUNS = 50
for _ in range(NUM_RUNS):
  b = time.perf_counter()
  size += [len(urllib.request.urlopen(request).read())]
  duration += [(time.perf_counter() - b) * 1000]

print("%d runs:" % NUM_RUNS)
print("size min/max/avg/stddev: %d/%d/%d/%d" % (
    min(size), max(size), statistics.mean(size), statistics.stdev(size)
))
print("duration min/max/avg/stddev: %d/%d/%d/%d" % (
    min(duration),
    max(duration),
    statistics.mean(duration),
    statistics.stdev(duration)
))
```

Without the feature-flag, the results look like this (YMMV):
```bash
> python3 test.py
50 runs:
size min/max/avg/stddev: 980436/980470/980450/17
duration min/max/avg/stddev: 22/47/31/5
```

with the feature-flag, the results looks like this:
```bash
50 runs:
size min/max/avg/stddev: 2465211/2465211/2465211/0
duration min/max/avg/stddev: 97/146/110/13
```

Investigation
==========

Since we can see that there is a clear difference between the two, let's try to profile the difference.

Let's send queries infinitely to the apiserver so we can see what it's doing:
```bash
while true
do curl --silent -H "Accept: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf" \
  http://localhost:8080/api/v1/pods >/dev/null
done
```

In a different window, start profiling:
```bash
go tool pprof http://localhost:8080/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30
... (wait)
> kcachegrind # If you don't know this, it's absolutely awesome.
```

![Screenshot from 2019-04-05 15-03-13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1929644/55658842-fc969400-57b3-11e9-99a6-0303fc4c3650.png)

Let's look at that method:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.14.0/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/generated.pb.go#L2107-L2120

It basically does a full tree traversal to know how big the buffer needs to be allocated, that's OK.

The problem is that this method is called again and again at every depth of the tree while serializing the map:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.14.0/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/generated.pb.go#L737-L774

which means that the marshaling complexity is going to be proportional to the square of the depth of the map.

My suspicion thought is that this problem is not limited to "maps", but to all objects we serialize in kubernetes, let's look at it:
Taking a random o
... [body truncated]

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #71592: Probe httpHeaders "Host" is lost after redirect

Issue description:
Hello there,

I did search around and didn't find a report for this already, I hope it's  not a dupe.

**What happened**:
In an HTTP probe definition (readyness or liveness), the custom host header is not set properly after a redirect occurs.

**What you expected to happen**:
Seeing that #18233 states that redirects are weird but allowed, I would expect the custom headers to be maintained after the redirect occurs.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Setup an HTTP service that expects a specific Host header to be used (using Django here) and would return a 400 if the Host doesn't match (for a more detail view at how Django deals with this [read along](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/2.1/ref/settings/#allowed-hosts)).

Then setup a probe like:

```
livenessProbe:
    httpGet:
        path: /admin/
        port: http
        httpHeaders:
            - name: Host
              value: the-expected-host.tld
```

You should now see in your logs that the first call to the service succeeded with a 301 (or 3XX) which means the Host header was set properly, but that the call to the redirected url will fail with a 400 which means the Host header was not set anymore and makes the probe raise an error.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
In the above test, setting the "path" to the redirected url works and the probe is green.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #78136: Cloudprovider AWS should query instance by ID when possible

Issue description:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Currently cloud provider package aws.go has many places to query ec2 instance by node name. #76749 has already optimized quite few inefficient tagging usages in the library.

Furthermore, since aws does not track ec2 instance by node name (node name is just a tag), querying instance by tag is not as efficient as querying instance by ID.

It will make k8s more efficient if k8s can convert nodeName to nodeID before actually making the cloud provider calls.

**Why is this needed**:
Currently `Cloud` interface already have kubeClient exposed to it, we can get `v1.Node` from api call and parse providerID, and issue cloud provider call with providerID directly. We tried such optimization internally and it can tremendously reduce the number of DescribeInstance calls and also make each DescribeInstance call much faster.

Also, because node querying has limited frequency, mostly during node controller reconciliation, and the only bursts are during batch infrastructure provisioning (i.e. create a batch of 100 PVC with ebs), load added to api server is limited, and can be optimized further by introducing informer interface to aws cloud provider.

/assign zhan849
/sig aws
/sig cloud-provider
/sig scalability

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Cloud provider AWS library should query instance by ID when possible
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature
/sig aws
/sig cloud-provider
/sig scalability

**What this PR does / why we need it:**
This PR changed the implementation of `getInstanceByNodeName()` in aws library to query instance from provider using instance id when possible, since it is much more efficient to get instance by ID in aws than run a filter. This PR checks if it is able to get provider id from `v1.Node`, if possible, it will get instance by node id, or it will fall back to running the query

We tested internally wit batch PVC provisioning benchmark and here are the improvements shown that makes k8s more scalable in aws environment:

- Reduced more than 90% DescribeInstance calls (1638 calls including lots of retries -> 116 calls all successful with batch size 50)
- Latency of each DescribeInstance call also got reduced
- Before this change, peak DescribeInstances QPS grows linearly and ~= batch size, with this change, peak DescribeInstances QPS stays stably at ~10 calls/sec

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes:**
Fixes #78136

This is also the first step towards fixing #78409 , by introduce informer-fed node cache to aws library.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**
Regarding the tradeoff of offloading the workload to kubernetes:
1. Node querying has limited frequency, mostly during node controller reconciliation, and the only bursts are during batch infrastructure provisioning (i.e. create a batch of 100 PVC with ebs, aggressive autoscaling by adding 100 nodes to cluster, etc). `Get()` calls are also relatively cheap. Therefore, load added to api server is limited, and can be optimized further by introducing informer interface to aws cloud provider

2. Usually in production, each aws account would have multiple Kubernetes clusters and other non-k8s clusters, but aws related api call throttles are account-wide, so that is to say, if one kubernetes cluster is making inefficient call to cloud provider, other k8s/non-k8s clusters will be affected as well. so it worth the tradeoff and affects of burst in k8s calls can be limited to k8s cluster level, with proper retry mechanism (which we already have) control plane can make progress eventually

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?:**
```
none
```


**Release note:**
```release-note
Optimize EC2 DescribeInstances API calls in aws cloud provider library by querying instance ID instead of EC2 filters when possible
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #78443: kube-proxy panics when parsing iptables-save output

Issue description:
On some systems, iptables-save outputs the following warning to stderr:
```
# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present, use iptables-legacy-save to see them
```

Note that the error message includes a newline.

Because kube-proxy captures both stdout and stderr when calling `iptables-save`, the newline might cause rules to be garbled. For example, the output might contain the following line:
```
:8443
```

The parser treats this as a chain line, and panics, as predicted in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/util/iptables/save_restore.go#L62-L63

Issue #78807: fakeTimer::Stop and Reset do not work

Issue description:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I was writing a variant of clock.FakeClock, and noticed a couple of bugs in `func (f *fakeTimer) Stop()`.  Look at the pointer comparison in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c7972d9a5e7f555371fec7a3237f08ebc1ae9d7c/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/clock/clock.go#L298 --- the two pointers will never be equal, but the author clearly expected equality when `i` is the index of the fakeClockWaiter corresponding to the fakeTimer.  The two pointers will never be equal because one is a pointer into the fakeClock's `waiters` slice while the other pointer is to a field of the `fakeTimer`.  The consequence of this bug is that the Stop function is ineffective.

Also, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c7972d9a5e7f555371fec7a3237f08ebc1ae9d7c/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/clock/clock.go#L305 determines the returned value based on the original copy of the waiter, which --- being a copy --- did not get updated if/when the waiter fired.

Note also that clock_test.go does not exercise FakeClock::NewTimer at all.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

There are various reasons that the HPA will decide not the change the current scale.  Two important ones are when missing metrics might change the direction of scaling, and when the recommended scale is within tolerance of the current scale.

The way that `ReplicaCalculator` signals it's desire to not change the current scale is by returning the current scale.  However the current scale is from `scale.Status.Replicas` and can be larger than `scale.Spec.Replicas` (e.g. during Deployment rollout with configured surge).  This causes a positive feedback loop because `scale.Status.Replicas` is written back into `scale.Spec.Replicas`, further increasing the current scale.

This PR fixes the feedback loop by plumbing the replica count from spec through `horizontal.go` and `replica_calculator.go` so the calculator can punt with the right value.

It also introduces separate types for replica counts derived from `scale.Spec` and `scale.Status` (`specReplicas` and `statusReplicas` respectively) to guard against this kind of cross-talk.  When returning a desired scale to be written into spec, the calculator must either return the given, current scale, or explicitly call `newSpecReplicas`.

With separate types, other sources of cross-talk became compiler errors.  E.g. [recording Status.Replicas as an initial recommendation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cb862e332329736dc1b893da6f757b808fa802aa/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go#L573-L574). **What would you like to be added**:
I would like the number of test images to be reduced and the documentation improved. The list is in this file:

The ways to reduce the image count include:

 - It makes it easier to understand which image you should choose if you are writing a new test and need some guidance

Issue #80146: events v1beta1: absence of optional `Related` event gives an error

Issue description:
Per the comments in v1beta1 Event:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7285829b8306a7cc1a2dc0da943afcfe45c06579/staging/src/k8s.io/api/events/v1beta1/types.go#L61-L64

The `Related` field claimed to be optional, but an error is dumped if it's illegal - including the `nil` case:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7285829b8306a7cc1a2dc0da943afcfe45c06579/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/events/event_recorder.go#L52-L55

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7285829b8306a7cc1a2dc0da943afcfe45c06579/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L440

If appropriate, I'm gonna raise a PR to tolerate the nil case. @yastij please advice.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #73235: Azure Load Balancer public IP lookup by name

Issue description:
**What would you like to be added**:
Add an annotation to allow lookup of loadBalancerIP by specifying a named Azure resource instead of an explicit IP address. This can pair with the existing 'azure-load-balancer-resource-group' annotation (perhaps call it 'azure-load-balancer-public-ip-resource' or similar).

**Why is this needed**:
During provisioning of k8s clusters on Azure we request IP addresses with specific tags from an Azure IP allocation service. As a result we do not know at cluster setup time what address we will receive, but we do know what the name of the resource is as we control this. While possible to look up the IP during YAML generation it feels more appropriate to extend this functionality within k8s itself.

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b6c8ef298ebfceb66422c416f55ab6076b7ff65d/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/azure/azure_loadbalancer.go#L213 it appears an attempt is made to do a reverse lookup from IP address to resource anyway so this would just save time/effort.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #80775: Allow Filter plugins of the scheduling framework to identify whether a pod could be schedulable after preemption

Issue description:
**What would you like to be added:**
`Filter` plugins of the scheduling framework need to indicate whether a pod that is unschedulable on a node could potentially be schedulable if one or more other existing pods are removed from the node. In other words, whether preemption can help make the pod schedulable. For example, a taint filter may return an "unresolvable" infeasibility for a node, because removal of other pods is not going to change taints, while a resource check filter return a "resovable" infeasibility.

One idea to address this problem is to add another [`Status.Code`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/75d51896125b1cafd9e995212b02ccda9b8a0aed/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1/interface.go#L48) for unresolvable infeasibility. We currently have `Unschedulable`. We can add something like `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` (or a better name). If a filter plugin returns this code for a node, the scheduler will not attempt preemption for that node.

Another idea is to put the information in the scheduler plugin config. For each filter plugin, the config indicates whether it is resolvable or not. This will act similar to what we [currently have in the scheduler code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/75d51896125b1cafd9e995212b02ccda9b8a0aed/pkg/scheduler/core/generic_scheduler.go#L65) (it is hard coded). This approach works well too, but it is static. The previous approach allows filter plugins to return different codes dynamically and depending on the conditions of the cluster. For example, a plugin that checks availability of resources may return `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` when it sees that the incoming pod has lower priority than all other existing pods on the node.

Please share your opinion about the two approaches or other proposals so that we can choose one to implement.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
ref/ kubernetes/enhancements#624

**What happened**:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod

      failureThreshold: 3
      initialDelaySeconds: 10
      periodSeconds: 10
      successThreshold: 1
      timeoutSeconds: 1
    livenessProbe:

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #83472: Duplicate Custom Predicates/Priorities

Issue description:
Currently custom predicate and priorities can be created through the [Policy API](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/api/v1/types.go#L51-L71).

The problem is that a custom predicate/priority, like ServiceAffinity, can be [listed](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/api/v1/types.go#L32-L35) multiple times in the Policy with different names, possibly with different arguments.

This semantic (i.e., specifying multiple instances of the same custom predicate with different arguments) is only useful if different ```Weight```s were specified because in all cases of custom predicates/priorities the arguments are merge-able (for example, ```Labels``` from multiple CheckServiceAffinity custom predicates can be merged into one set).

In the world of framework plugins, we don't currently have a way to maintain those semantics. [```PluginConfig```](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go#L98), which specifies plugins' arguments is separate from list that specifies which [```Plugins```](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go#L91) to run.

The question here: do we really want to maintain the old semantics of custom predicates and priorities? in other words, do we need to change the ComponentConfig API to somehow allow specifying multiple instances of the same Plugin with different arguments/weights, or should we consider that this is not supported?

I always lean towards simplifying things, so my suggestion is to not support that, but I would like to know if there are actual deployments that rely on this.


/sig scheduling

/cc @bsalamat @misterikkit @Huang-Wei @k82cn @ravisantoshgudimetla

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #84041: Kube-proxy should support setting ipvs tcp/tcpfin/udp timeout when proxy-mode is ipvs

Issue description:
**What would you like to be added**:
kube-proxy can add three new options to set the ipvs tcp/tcpfin/udp timeout when proxy-mode is ipvs, such as:
``` shell
# kube-proxy new options
--ipvs-tcp-timeout duration
--ipvs-tcpfin-timeout duration
--ipvs-udp-timeout duration

# corresponding to the settings below
root@my-master01:~# ipvsadm -ln --timeout
Timeout (tcp tcpfin udp): 900 120 300
```

**Why is this needed**:
kube-proxy has some options to set kernel parameters related to netfilter conntrack, such as:
`net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` can be set by `--conntrack-tcp-timeout-established`
`net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait` can be set by `--conntrack-tcp-timeout-close-wait`

So, when kube-proxy's proxy-mode is ipvs, we also want to set the ipvs tcp/tcpfin/udp timeout by kube-proxy.

currently, we can only set it through the command, like `ipvsadm --set 900 120 60`, but when k8s node is restarted, these changes will be invalid(of course, use rc.local or systemd is also a way)

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: support configuration of kube-proxy IPVS tcp,tcpfin,udp timeout
PR description:
Signed-off-by: Andrew Sy Kim <kiman@vmware.com>

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR allows IPVS tcp, tcpfin and udp timeouts to be configurable via kube-proxy flags/config.

The following flags are being added:
```
--ipvs-tcp-timeout <duration>
--ipvs-tcpfin-timeout <duration>
--ipvs-udp-timeout <duration>
```

The flags above are equivalent to running the following `ipvsadm` command on any linux node:
```
ipvsadm --set <tcp-timeout> <tcpfin-timeout> <udp-timeout>
```

`ipvsadm --set` according to the [ipvsadm man page](https://linux.die.net/man/8/ipvsadm):
```
--set tcp tcpfin udp
    Change the timeout values used for IPVS connections. This command always takes 3 parameters, representing the timeout values (in seconds) for TCP sessions, TCP sessions after receiving a FIN packet, and UDP packets, respectively. A timeout value 0 means that the current timeout value of the corresponding entry is preserved.
```
The default values for the new kube-proxy flags are 0 because passing in 0 to `ipvsadm --set` means the current timeout value on the system is preserved.

**What happened**: Using a pod like the nginx-ing-cntlr with an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB), and then draining the node its running on to force a migration to another node pool, does not reliably deregister the drained nodes from the NLB Target group. This causes the nodeport used by the NLB to remain open, and the drained node ends up continuing to funnel traffic for other pods cause of `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` being used. Issue #86410: AAD token obtained by kubectl has spn prefix which is incompatible with AAD on-behalf-of flow

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/

**What happened**:
In the [code path](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/search?q=NewOAuthConfig&unscoped_q=NewOAuthConfig) to acquire AAD token, because of the inclusion of the API version in the URLs for authorization, the returned token is not compatible with many AAD scenarios like OIDC and On-Behalf-Of flow.

There is a long list of issues documenting this problem:
https://github.com/Azure/go-autorest/issues/277
https://github.com/Azure/go-autorest/issues/321
https://github.com/AzureAD/azure-activedirectory-library-for-nodejs/issues/128
https://github.com/AzureAD/azure-activedirectory-library-for-python/pull/57
https://github.com/Azure/aks-engine/issues/376

The fix is pretty simple, use [this api](https://github.com/Azure/go-autorest/blob/2913f263500c4a5b23dada1b46ccd22ac972315f/autorest/adal/config.go#L56) with `apiVersion` set to `nil`.

This incompatible behavior impacts
https://github.com/appscode/guard/issues/131
https://github.com/appscode/guard/issues/235

**What you expected to happen**:
Follow the [official documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/v1-protocols-oauth-code#use-the-authorization-code-to-request-an-access-token) to acquire AAD token

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
use kubectl to get AAD token, paste token into https://jwt.ms/ and verify the audience claim

Issue #86089: Write listCoreV1ServiceForAllNamespaces Mock Test for Conformance - +1 coverage

Issue description:
This issue proposes the writing of a new test for the `listCoreV1ServiceForAllNamespaces` API endpoint with the intention of promoting it to Conformance. This issue contains a very basic **mock** test in order to start the conversation about what a good e2e test would look like for this endpoint. The code below is verified to be hitting the intended endpoint, show as per the queries in APIsnoop's live view of the cluster's audit logs.

## Our Kubectl Apply

```shell
kubectl apply -f "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cncf/apisnoop/master/deployment/k8s/raiinbow.yaml" --namespace=kube-system
```

# Identify a Feature Using APISnoop

There are no tests listing services, see the following:

```sql-mode
SELECT
  operation_id, path, description
  FROM untested_stable_core_endpoints
  where operation_id like 'list%'
  and path like '/api/v1/services' ;
```

```sql-mode
           operation_id            |       path       |              description
-----------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------------------
 listCoreV1ServiceForAllNamespaces | /api/v1/services | list or watch objects of kind Service
(1 row)

```

# API documentation
- [godocs - ServiceInterface](https://godoc.org/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/typed/core/v1#ServiceInterface)
- [typed/core/v1/service.go#L45](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/kubernetes/typed/core/v1/service.go#L45)

# My Mock Test

```shell
go get -v -u k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1
go get -v -u k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes
go get -v -u k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd
```

This mock test uses client-go's functions and hits the endpoints.

```go
// uses the current context in kubeconfig
kubeconfig := flag.String("kubeconfig",
  fmt.Sprintf("%v/%v/%v", os.Getenv("HOME"), ".kube", "config"),
  "(optional) absolute path to the kubeconfig file")
flag.Parse()
config, err := clientcmd.BuildConfigFromFlags("", *kubeconfig)
if err != nil {
  fmt.Println(err)
}
// make our work easier to find in the audit_event queries
config.UserAgent = "live-test-pod-count"
// creates the clientset
clientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(config)
// access the API to list services in all namespaces
svcs, _ := clientset.CoreV1().Services("").List(v1.ListOptions{})

foundSvc := false
for _, svc := range svcs.Items {
  if svc.ObjectMeta.Name == "kubernetes" {
    foundSvc = true
  }
}

if foundSvc == false {
  fmt.Println("[status] could NOT find service in service list in all namespaces")
  return
}

fmt.Println("[status] found service in list of services in all namespaces")
```

# Verify with APISnoop

This shows the endpoints hit by my approach:

```sql-mode

```sql-mode

 live-test-pod-count | listCoreV1ServiceForAllNamespaces |          0 |               1
(1 row)

```

select * from projected_change_in_coverage;
```

```sql-mode
   category    | total_endpoints | old_coverage | new_coverage | change_in_number
---------------|-----------------|--------------|--------------|------------------
 test_coverage |             438 |          183 |          184 |                1
(1 row)

```

Issue #87541: Update Azure auth module in kubectl to obtain proper audience claim in AAD token

Issue description:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
add a flag in Azure auth module in kubectl to get AAD token with audience claim in proper (most commonly accepted) format.

**Why is this needed**:
The original issue is explained very well in #86410. In sort, the current `azure` auth module will get a token whose `audience` claim has `spn:` prefix. This prefix is not documented in most Azure AD documentation which causes confusion and blocks some scenario.

There was an attempt to update existing `azure` auth module in #86412 which resulted in a breaking behavior to existing k8s clusters using Azure AD OIDC. The issue is documented well in #87464. Hence, the #86412 PR is reverted in #87507.

As discussed in [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87464#issuecomment-577894188), a proper migration path to achieve #86410 with zero impact to existing clusters should be:
1. (client side change) add a flag in azure auth module in kubectl to allow new behavior
2. (server side change) update api server to support multiple `--oidc-client-id`
3. customers can opt in to update `--oidc-client-id=spn:<guid>;<guid>` so that kubectl in old and new can still authenticate with api-server
4. migrate kubectl/kubeconfig to use new flag
5. update `--oidc-client-id=<guid>`

This issue is to implement the first task: **(client side change) add a flag in azure auth module in kubectl to allow new behavior**

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #83476: TopologyManager: Guarantee Aligned resources for Multiple Containers

Issue description:
The `TopologyManager` is currently only guaranteed to work if a _single_ container in the pod spec requires aligned resources.

The reason for this is the following:

* The admit handler for the `TopologyManager` loops through all containers, calling out to the `CPUManager` and `devicemanager` to generate hints for each of them individually, rather than on the entire pod as a whole.

* Generating hints relies on looking at the current resource request and considering the current allocation state to figure out what the appropriate set of hints to send back should be.

* However, the admit handler in the `TopologyManager` is called strictly before the `CPUManager` and `devicemanager` have the opportunity to do any device allocation.

* This results in unreliable hint generation for all but the first container, since subsequent containers have no idea what the allocation state will be once that first container is allocated some resources.

This can be solved in one of two ways:

1. Change the pod admit handler for the `TopologyManager` to loop through each container, first calling out to the `CPUManager` and `devicemanager` to generate hints and then immediately calling out to perform device allocation in the same iteration of the loop.

1. Change the `TopologyManager` to do hint generation at the pod level rather than the container level. It is unclear if this is desirable, however, since each container should be able to have its resources aligned separately, and not forced to a single alignment for all resources across the entire pod.

Option (1) seems like the better option, but it will require significant updates to both the `CPUManager` and the `devicemanager`. The `CPUManager` will need to be updated to support CPU allocation at pod admit time (currently it is done at container start time). The `devicemanager` will need to be updated to allocate devices on a container-by-container basis. Currently, it loops through the resource list for all containers at once and allocates devices to them accordingly.

As we iterate on a solution to this, we should update the existing KEPs for the [CPUManager](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/node/cpu-manager.md) and [TopologyManager](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/0035-20190130-topology-manager.md) with the proposed changes.

Tracking PRs:
~~https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84196 Refactor parts of CPUManager~~
~~https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84462 Update CPUManager state information~~
~~https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84300 Update logic in `CPUManager` `reconcileState()`~~
TBD Refactor devicemanager Allocate / UpdatePluginResources logic
TBD Move CPU allocation to pod admit time instead of container start time
TBD Update the `devicemanager` to allocate devices on a container-by-container basis
TBD Move TopologyHint generation and final resource allocation into the same synchronous loop

Issue #87854: kube-proxy can panic if len(HealthzBindAddresses) == 0

Issue description:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

`kube-proxy`, from whatever combination of inputs we stuck into it, segfaulted. The segfault, which originates from a slightly modified fork of v1.17, looks as such:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x20 pc=0x3d1c786]
goroutine 149 [running]:
k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/proxy/healthcheck.(*ProxierHealthServer).Updated(0x0)
        /go/src/kubernetes/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/proxy/healthcheck/proxier_health.go:83 +0x26
k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/proxy/iptables.(*Proxier).SyncLoop(0xc00014db00)
        /go/src/kubernetes/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go:474 +0x62
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kube-proxy/app.(*ProxyServer).Run(0xc0001fc480, 0xc0004acc60, 0xc0004acc60)
        /go/src/kubernetes/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go:714 +0x735
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kube-proxy/app.(*Options).runLoop.func1(0xc0002b1a80)
        /go/src/kubernetes/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go:324 +0x34
created by k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kube-proxy/app.(*Options).runLoop
        /go/src/kubernetes/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go:323 +0x50
```

Translated to master, where the problem appears to be present, the segfault originates from this call:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d90dd93855ab6c3ccda73dfbd3d19c81f56abca5/pkg/proxy/healthcheck/proxier_health.go#L89

And that is called from here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d90dd93855ab6c3ccda73dfbd3d19c81f56abca5/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L512-L514

This seems odd, because

* The only pointer involved in the segfaulting call is `hs` itself
* The caller nil-checks before calling a method on `hs`.

I did some digging and found #49137, which is a fix for this problem. However, this fix appears to be undone in #83498. There doesn't seem to be a reason for this to have been changed in the latter PR.

**What you expected to happen**:

PR title: Don't try to create VolumeSpec immediately after underlying PVC is being deleted
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
As @mm4tt mentioned in #86434, when PVC is being deleted, desired_state_of_world_populator shouldn't try to create VolumeSpec.

This PR is a performance bug fix.

The fix is rebased on @jingxu97 's comment:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86670#issuecomment-569823371

Original proposal is to add map pvcsUnderDeletion to desiredStateOfWorldPopulator.
The map is from namespaced claim name to the earliest time when next GET request to api-server is made.
The proposal is able to handle generic api server error return and limits the change within desired_state_of_world_populator.go

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #86434

```release-note
Fix that prevents repeated fetching of PVC/PV objects by kubelet when processing of pod volumes fails. While this prevents hammering API server in these error scenarios, it means that some errors in processing volume(s) for a pod could now take up to 2-3 minutes before retry.
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #88494: Daemonset pod status PATCH errors after upgrading cluster from 1.14 to 1.16

Issue description:
**What happened**:

The cluster master in a Kubernetes v1.14.10 cluster was upgraded to V1.16.7.  The process of upgrading nodes is under way and has been spread over a week so far.  The cluster owner reported seeing a high percentage of pod status PATCH failures.  The apiserver logs show errors like:
```
I0223 20:40:57.482215       1 httplog.go:90] PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/cache-images-2-10-2/pods/dashdb-daemonset-s4crw/status: (8.261945ms) 500
...
logging error output: "k8s\x00\n\f\n\x02v1\x12\x06Status\x12b\n\x06\n\x00\x12\x00\x1a\x00\x12\aFailure\x1aJconversion Error: v1.PodIP(172.30.147.226) != v1.PodIPs[0](172.30.147.223)\"\x000\xf4\x03\x1a\x00\"\x00"
 [hyperkube/v1.14.5+IKS (linux/amd64) kubernetes/7bc6122 172.16.25.64:65323]
```

The errors are all from the v1.14 nodes and have all been for pods associated with DaemonSets.

We don't yet know why pods' IPs are changing, but it appears that pod status patches that include a changed `PodIP` result in an object where `PodIPs[]` contains the old IP, and `podIP` has the new IP. We believe this is because `PodIPs[]` was introduced in Kubernetes v1.15 and the patch request from a v1.14 node results in both `PodIP=new IP` and `PodIPs = [old IP]` being present in the result.

If you aren't monitoring for request failures it may not obvious that any error is occurring: The pods continue to show their last successfully reported state.  Deleting such pods, however, results in the pod being stuck in a `Terminating` state.

We are only seeing this for DaemonSet pods - I suspect because whatever resulted in pod IPs changing also causes non-DaemonSet pods to be deleted and recreated.

We have a number of cluster still on v1.14 that we expect to upgrade to v1.15 or v1.16.

**What you expected to happen**:

Kubernetes v1.14 nodes should be able to update pod status during the transition from v1.14 to v1.16 even if pod IPs change during that time.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

We have recreated this in the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service by "reloading" nodes.  The reload process leaves the Kubernetes node object in place, and essentially reloads the image with the proper kubeconfig to rejoin the cluster.  The cluster I was debugging does not appear to have had nodes "reloaded" - something else is triggering the pod IP changes.

- Create a v1.14 cluster
- Deploy a DaemonSet (anything with pod networking should suffice)
- Upgrade cluster master to v1.16
- Reload a v1.14 node.

One the node is back up, `crictl inspectp` shows the pod's network IP has changed.  Kubelet and apiserver logs show the errors describe earlier.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.14.x (nodes) and v1.16.7 (master)
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): 18.04.4 LTS
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.15.0-76-generic
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Honor status.podIP over status.podIPs and node.spec.podCIDR over node.spec.PodCIDRs when mismatched
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind api-change
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

### When status.podIP and status.podIPs[0] do not agree, honor status.podIP as the older API field, rather than failing to convert.

This is required to support Kubelets < 1.16 running against API servers >= 1.16.

Kubelets >= 1.16 set both podIP and podIPs:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1386-L1396

Kubelets < 1.16 only set podIP:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.15/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1384-L1385

However, since kubelets update pod status with a patch API request, existing unknown fields are preserved. That means a 1.15 kubelet, when trying to modify a podIP, will only update the podIP field and not podIPs.

### When node.spec.podCIDR and node.spec.podCIDRs[0] do not agree, honor node.spec.podCIDR as the older API field, rather than failing to convert.

prior to 1.16, the rangeAllocator and cloudCIDRAllocator controllers updated node.spec.podCIDR using a patch:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.15/pkg/controller/nodeipam/ipam/adapter.go#L92-L106

in 1.16+, there are three methods to update node specs, all of which use patch:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/util/node/node.go#L194-L207
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/util/node/node.go#L179-L186
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.16/pkg/controller/nodeipam/ipam/adapter.go#L94-L106

These patch methods either just set the old node.spec.podCIDR field, or they set both the old and new podCIDR/podCIDRs field (for paths that are multi-CIDR-aware).

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #88494

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
Fixes a regression with clients prior to 1.15 not being able to update podIP in pod status, or podCIDR in node spec, against >= 1.16 API servers
```

/cc @thockin @khenidak
/sig network

Issue #87784: Define in-tree PluginConfig Args as component config types

Issue description:
/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

As we move from parameters in the root of the component config to using args in PluginConfig (#87617), we are losing visibility of available parameters (in the API definition) and their early validation. Arguably, we might also lose versioning.

Since the configuration of in-tree plugins is part of the API, one alternative is to move the args definition to the `pkg/scheduler/apis/config` package and their versioned counterparts.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #73972: Slow volume attach for single ReadOnlyMany volume across multiple nodes

Issue description:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!-->


**What happened**: A GCE PD volume is used in read-only mode (through a PVC & PV pair in ReadOnlyMany mode) by over 100 pods running across tens of nodes. Volume attachment sometimes takes over 30min for some of these pods.

**What you expected to happen**: Attaching should take seconds instead of minutes.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
* Provision a read-only GCE PD, and the associated PVC & PV.
* Run a Job with parallelism of 100+ pods in a cluster with tens of nodes (we tested with 50+), and use the PD inside all pods.

**Anything else we need to know?**: Generally attach/detach calls are parallelized (through OperationExecutor), but calls with the same volume name are serialized. This was done as a way to prevent races between attach and detach calls for the same volume. However, it's sufficient to provide this guarantee for each node, as long as the volume is Read[Write|Only]Many.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f96849981203ea506ea8fa3f88c173d36cf688aa/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_executor.go#L607-L608

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): Tested with multiple 1.10 patch releases (including 1.10.6 and 1.10.9)
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: GCP

/sig storage
/priority critical-urgent
/assign
/cc @davidz627 @jingxu97 @msau42 @saad-ali

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #88868: SystemOOMs not reported for containers

Issue description:
**What happened**:

A SystemOOM event was not reported even when the memory limit hit was the root cgroup memory limit.

**What you expected to happen**:

A SystemOOM event should have been reported.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Do not set `--system-reserved` or `--kube-reserved`, and set `--eviction-hard=` to disable memory eviction on the kubelet.  Run a pod without memory limits which slowly consumes memory, such as with `k8s.gcr.io/stress:v1` from https://github.com/vishh/stress.  Use arguments -mem-alloc-size", "100Mi", "-mem-alloc-sleep", "10s".  This should trigger an OOM on the root cgroup, but no event will be generated.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

cAdvisor populates ContainerName and VictimContainerName from matching the regexp: [`Task in (.*) killed as a result of limit of (.*)`](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/blob/master/utils/oomparser/oomparser.go#L29).  A SystemOOM should mean VictimContainerName == "/", as we are looking for OOMs that are "killed as a results of limit of /".  However, we incorrectly [check ContainerName](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/oom/oom_watcher_linux.go#L75) instead in the kubelet.

cc @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs @derekwaynecarr @sjenning @dchen1107

**What happened**:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/85735 introduces a regression that `getNodeAddressesByProviderIDOrName` func is invoked on a Node obj without `.spec.providerID`, hence it can fail fetching the node addresses when the `.spec.providerID` is not set.

**What you expected to happen**:
I would expect cloud-controller-manager to be able to initialize new Node.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Start the gcp legacy-cloud-controller v1.18.1 (`--cloud-provider="gce"`)

2. Ensure that the node-controller cannot initialize a new Node. Logs of the cloud-controller-manager repeated multiple times:
```
I0410 15:48:51.287480       1 node_controller.go:325] Initializing node shoot--foo--bar-cpu-worker-z1-68f57cffcd-dbq47 with cloud provider
E0410 15:48:51.295679       1 gce_instances.go:575] Failed to fetch instanceID via Metadata: metadata: GCE metadata "instance/hostname" not defined
E0410 15:48:51.541680       1 node_controller.go:370] failed to initialize node shoot--foo--bar-cpu-worker-z1-68f57cffcd-dbq47 at cloudprovider: error fetching node by provider ID: error splitting providerID, and error by node name: couldn't get internal IP: metadata: GCE metadata "instance/network-interfaces/0/ip" not defined

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #90211: agnhost/netexec test image supports HTTPS

Issue description:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

The `agnhost` image used in E2E tests is used for testing a wide variety of OS-agnostic features. One of these is `netexec`, which runs an HTTP server with various endpoints that can be used to validate things like request/response.

It would be useful to allow for `agnhost`'s `netexec` functionality to also support HTTPS so all of that logic can be tested for TLS-based traffic.

Currently, `netexec` can be run like:
```bash
/agnhost netexec --http-port 8080
```

I'm proposing something along the lines of:
```bash
/agnhost netexec --http-port 8443 --tls-cert-file "/cert.pem" --tls-private-key-file "/key.pem"
```

The default certificate/private key being basically identical to what [agnhost/porter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/images/agnhost#porter) provides.

**Why is this needed**:

One use case is #86139 where the intent is to add HTTPS functionality to lifecycle hooks (postStart/preStop). There is currently no easy way to test this logic because the container which receives the HTTPS request (in this case, `agnhost/netexec`) does not support HTTPS traffic.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Adds HTTPS logic to agnhost netexec
PR description:
The agnhost image used for testing has a `netexec` path which supports
two new flags, `--tls-cert-file` and `--tls-private-key-file`. If the
former is provided, the HTTP server will be upgraded to HTTPS, using the
certificate (and private key) provided.

By default, there are keys already mounted into the container at
`/localhost.crt` and `/localhost.key`, which contain PEM-encoded TLS
certs with IP SANs for `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`.

PR title: [v1.18] Move ipvs lib to third_party/forked and fix address family bug present in old kernels
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
There's a bug in `github.com/docker/libnetwork/ipvs` where an address cannot be parsed because the netlink address family attribute is not set (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89520). This bug is only present in old kernels (<3.18). There's a fix for this bug in moby/ipvs [v1.0.1](https://github.com/moby/ipvs/releases/tag/v1.0.1), however, we can't cherry-pick that fix for v1.18 since we are still vendoring docker/libnetwork. We also can't fix `github.com/docker/libnetwork/ipvs` since it was removed in favor of `github.com/moby/ipvs` and we don't want to update the release branch to use `github.com/moby/ipvs` since that involves bumping `github.com/vishvananda/netlink` to `v1.1.0` which introduces some significant changes to other components.

In order to cherry-pick the bug fix without significant changes to vendored dependencies, this PR:
* moves `vendor/github.com/docker/libnetwork/ipvs` -> `third_party/forked/ipvs`
* removes `github.com/docker/libnetwork` from go.mod
* update imports to `k8s.io/kubernetes/third_party/forked/ipvs`
* fix the address family bug based on fixes that went into moby/ipvs@v1.0.1 (https://github.com/moby/ipvs/pull/15 and https://github.com/moby/ipvs/pull/19)
* some other changes required to get the IPVS e2e presubmit passing since this was only enabled/working starting in v1.19 (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/89327 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/89854)

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #89443: Parallelize prepulling all images in `e2e_node` tests

Issue description:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Unless disabled, the `test/e2e_node` tests will prepull all images when running. They do so using the [PrePullAllImages function](https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes@master/-/blob/test/e2e_node/image_list.go#L138).

I think there's the opportunity to improve the runtime of the test suite by prepulling the images in parallel.

**Why is this needed**:
Its always nicer to have faster tests :) Specifically for users running `make test-e2e-node` locally, it's nice to have the image prepull occur as quick as possible.

That being said, we should also be cognizant of any tradeoffs associated with prepulling the images in parallel. If the code is substantially more complex, we would need a large improvement in test speed to justify it. I'm hopeful this discussion could be had once we have a proof of concept diff (which I think should be fairly minimal effort to create).

Issue #90570: GCE "baremetal" cluster, worker node IPs not populated when kubelet --node-ip given IP of not-first-NIC

Issue description:
**What happened**:

when initializing a kubernetes cluster in Google Cloud manually (not using GKE), internal (and external if available/applicable) node IP is not populated in "kubectl get nodes" if the interface used to connect to the master and passed to kubelet does not correspond to the first network interface, nic0 on google cloud console UI.

I cannot "kubectl edit node" and patch in the node IP information into the "addresses" field either.

This issue does not occur when kubelet --node-ip=(ip of nic0).
kubelet on all members of the cluster declare cloud-provider="gce".

**What you expected to happen**:

when kubelet is given a node-ip argument, it is checked against all nics of the google cloud instance and populated in node information even if a nic other than nic0 is used.
Or at least I am allowed to override nodeIP somehow after the node is brought up.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
We have scripts that automate this "manual kubernetes" process, I will describe it as generally as I can but i can share chunks of the script as needed.
Given two VPCs,
initialize an instance for master, one nic on VPC1
initialize an instance for worker with two nics, one on VPC2, the other on VPC1.
install required dependencies on both (apt-get docker-ce kubelet kubeadm kubectl ...)
on master, mkdir -p /etc/default/kubelet; echo "KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--cloud-provider='gce' > /etc/default/kubelet; kubeadm init
on worker, mkdir -p /etc/default/kubelet; echo "KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--node-ip=(nic1 ip) --cloud-provider='gce' >/etc/default/kubelet; kubeadm join
wait a bit.
kubectl get nodes -o wide, verify no internal IP or external IP information is populated for the worker
journalctl -xef on worker to see something like
15855 kubelet_node_status.go:520] Failed to set some node status fields: failed to get node address from cloud provider that matches ip: (nic1 ip)

**Anything else we need to know?**:
i'm guessing the problem stems from something like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f7907083c21a1ad5af260a6f6887503c2566abfb/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/gce/gce_instances.go#L86

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L97
only loops through nic0's info, doesn't match, and then we return an error.
if the first bit returned an array of IPs instead of just a single set, that would probably fix this.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #91249: Extra scheduling attempts when other controllers update Pod Conditions

Issue description:
**What happened**:

An extra scheduling attempt is observed in some scenarios when kube-scheduler already has already assumed a pod and this has entered the binding routine.

If, during this time, a pod update is received, the pod is added back to the scheduling queue, even if binding succeeds. This is the correct behavior, as scheduling conditions might change. However this updates could just be unrelated status updates, such as updates to pod conditions.

We observe an extra scheduling attempt, which is visible in the log line:

```
Error scheduling default/pod-x: pod pod-x is in the cache, so can't be assumed; retrying
```

Which indicates that an attempt was made when the pod was already scheduled.

**What you expected to happen**:

No extra scheduling attempts

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

This depends on other controllers running on the cluster that might report pod conditions. One such controller is https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-gce

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Skips updates in Pod Conditions so that there is no extra scheduling attempt when other controllers update Conditions while pod is binding.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #91249

```release-note

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #85677: Scheduler does not clear nominatedNodeName on Pod when node is no longer valid

Issue description:
**What happened**:

Scheduler decided that it wants to schedule Pod P on Node N after preempting some pods from N.
It set the P.nominatedNodeName to N. After a while (before scheduling actually happened) node N was removed from the cluster.
Scheduler did not reset P.nominatedNodeName to empty value.

**What you expected to happen**:

I would expect scheduler to unset P.nominatedNodeName when the node is no longer valid.
The trivial reason for node not being valid any more is it is removed from the cluster.
But there are more cases to cover. Out of the top of my head I may think of:
- extra Pod was scheduled to node and there is not enough resources any more
  - either scheduled by scheduler
  - or directly as static pod/daemonset
- node became unschedulable

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

We did not try to reproduce issue manually. Yet following setup should work.
- create cluster with nodes A and B.
- ensure all system pods are running on A. Fill up A so it does not have spare resources.
- add a low priority Pod L with long termination, with requests matching allocatable of B. It should be scheduled to B.
- add a high priority Pod H. It should get B as nominatedNodeName
- kill node B
- the H.nominatedNodeName will still point to B which is no longer in the cluster

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Current behavior does not play well with Cluster Autoscaler which assumes that Pod with nominatedNodeName will be scheduled in a while.
Therefore such pods do not trigger scale-up. If we can have P.nominatedNodeName set incorrectly for unbounded period of time CA will never
provision node for P to run.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):

We observed the behavior during presubmit tests which run k8s built from HEAD of master on 27.11.2019.

Versions logged in test log:

Issue #91888: aws: Fix address sorting of non-contiguous interfaces

Issue description:
**What happened**:

#80747 does not handle "holes" in interface device-number correctly, dropping later interfaces.

Create instance with eth0, eth1, eth2 ENIs as usual.  Remove (eg: by selectively deleting pods) eth1.  Only the addresses on eth0 are reported by NodeAddresses.

**What you expected to happen**:

Addresses on eth0 and eth2 should be reported.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: aws: Fix address sorting of multiple interfaces
PR description:
It is common to have "holes" in the network interfaces, eg after
attaching eth1+eth2, and then removing eth1.

Make the sorting code from #80747 robust to this situation, and add a test that exposes the issue in the original code.

Fixes #91888

/kind bug
/sig aws
/sig cloud-provider

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

Theoretically, this is an important bug and should be backported.  Nobody has noticed however, so I think this reinforces my long-standing suspicion that nothing uses addresses other than the first InternalIP and we should just remove the rest from Kubernetes..  I leave the backport/no-backport decision up to somebody else :stuck_out_tongue:

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #89995: Unexpected startupProbe behavior.

Issue description:
If I have `startupProbe` probe and `readinessProbe` then all good. Previous version of the pod is terminated after startup probe success, but if  `readinessProbe` wasn't specified the pod becomes ready immediately. It would be nice to add new state (for example starting) which would have pods until a `startupProbe` is successful. Also, it would mean that container not ready for connection.

Thank you for attention!

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Pods which have not "started" can not be "ready"
PR description:
Before this commit, containers which have both a `startupProbe` and a
`readinessProbe` are marked as `ready=false` during stratup, but
containers which have only a `startupProbe` are marked `ready=true`.
This doesn't make sense.

This commit only considers readiness if the container is considered to
have "started", which leaves `ready=false` while starting up.

/kind bug

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #93106: Azure cloud provider hits the VMSS VMs List API more than it should

Issue description:
**What happened**:

Running a non-AKS k8s v1.18.5  cluster on Azure, with 50 VMSS attached (each containing one or two nodes).

When we do attach several new VMSSes, or create/replace several nodes, the controller-managed gets quickly throttled by Azure API, for instance like so:
```
kube-controller-manager[2014310]: E0708 08:33:13.752989 2014310 azure_vmss.go:570]
VirtualMachineScaleSetsClient.List failed:
&{true 0 2020-07-08 08:34:43.665286837 +0000 UTC m=+1598.271278798
azure cloud provider throttled for operation VMSSList with reason "client throttled"}
```

Having a closer look at the cloud provider code, we see controller-manager would re-scan all attached VMSS on cache miss or expired TTL. Not just the one that needs a refresh.

**What you expected to happen**:

Number of VMSS List calls should be linear (eg. one for a new instance's showing up or being deleted), and not O(number of vmss).

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Attach many VMSS (even if they contain a single VM) to a cluster, then attach more or create many pods with remote PVs.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.18.5
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Azure
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 20.04
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.4.0
- Controller-manager cloud-config:
```
{
  "subscriptionId": "xxx",
  "resourceGroup": "yyy",
  "location": "westus2",
  "vnetName": "www",
  "vnetResourceGroup": "zzz",
  "vmType": "vmss",
  "loadBalancerSku": "standard",
  "useManagedIdentityExtension": true,
  "excludeMasterFromStandardLB": true,
  "useInstanceMetadata": true,
  "cloudConfigType": "file",
  "vmssCacheTTLInSeconds": 900,
  "vmssVirtualMachinesCacheTTLInSeconds": 900,
  "vmCacheTTLInSeconds": 900
}
```

/kind bug
/sig cloud-provider
/area provider/azure

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Azure: use per-vmss vmssvm incremental cache
PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Azure's cloud provider VMSS VMs API accesses are mediated through a cache holding and refreshing all VMSS together.

Due to that we hit VMSSVM.List API more often than we could: an instance's cache miss or expiration should only require a single VMSS re-list, while it's currently O(n) relative to the number of attached Scale Sets.

Under hard pressure (clusters with many attached VMSS that can't all be listed in one sequence of successive API calls) the controller manager might be stuck trying to re-list everything from scratch, then aborting the whole operation due to rate limits, affecting the whole Subscription.

This patch replaces the global VMSS VMs cache by per-VMSS VMs caches.  Refreshes (VMSS VMs lists) are scoped to the single relevant VMSS; under severe throttling the various caches can be incrementally refreshed.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #93106

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

We are assuming VMSS nodes are named from VMSS' computerNamePrefix+id (or vmssName+id, when computerNamePrefix isn't specified), as described [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/virtual-machine-scale-sets-instance-ids](here) and [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.compute/2018-10-01/virtualmachinescalesets#virtualmachinescalesetosprofile-object](there). Are there special cases not covered by that doc? if so we can probably complement that optimistic lookup (trying the vmss matching name prefix first, happy path) by a fallback to a scan over remaining scale sets. The non-optimal fallback path would still be an improvement as (in case of throttling) we keep partial results (per VMSS caches), refreshes are incremental.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Azure: per VMSS VMSS VMs cache to prevent throttling on clusters having many attached VMSS
```

-->

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The Job controller currently uses `NumRequeues` to decide wether or not the job has exceeded the backoffLimit. `NumRequeues` represents the number of times a job has been requeued, a requeue can occur due to several reasons and not only for Fail events. This makes backoffLimit unpredictable.

This PR sets the job controller to use the number of `Failed` pods to decide if the job has exceeded the backoffLimit.

According to the documentation: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/apps/job.md#backoff-policy-and-failed-pod-limit

> For Never we count actual pod failures (reflected in .status.failed field). With OnFailure, we take an approximate value of pod restarts (as reported in .status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount).

For restart policy of `OnFailure` - the logic is handled in `pastBackoffLimitOnFailure` as described above.
For restart policy of `Never` - this PR fixes the logic to be as described above.

This solution has been discussed in the past by @janetkuo  in: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/70251#issuecomment-433507671

Issue #63906: Autogenerated container port name conflicts with multiple hostports

Issue description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug

**What happened**:

A container ports spec such as:
```
        ports:
        - containerPort: 4443
          hostPort: 443
        - containerPort: 4443
          hostPort: 4443
```
Results in this error:
```
kubelet[11270]: W0515 17:44:41.623947   11270 helpers.go:352] Port name conflicted, "cntr-TCP:4443" is defined more than once
```
From https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/container/helpers.go#L321 . Because of this, the port mappings are not setup correctly on the host when using a CNI-compliant portmap solution.

**What you expected to happen**:
Auto-generated port names should never result in duplicates

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
[d2.yml.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/1897012/d2.yml.txt)

PR description:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR is a replacement for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80470 (by @zouyee). It relaxes the validation in kubelet before passing node port mappings to CNI. Stated use case for this is to allow port transition for daemons. So both ports (old and new) are configured for the transition period and after some time old port being removed.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes  #63906

There is a question of whether this deduplication of port mappings is needed at all. For example, once the mapping is named, no duplication is happening and needs to be handled by CNI anyway. But removing this deduplication is a bigger change that may require a larger announcement and can potentially affect payload.

This PR also includes the relaxing of deduplication by hostIP. Similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94382 Same port is allows to be configured on different IPs.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #90652: Reduce the number of calls to GCE API (for clusters on GCE) coming from cloud node-controller

Issue description:
For external cloud provider - Kubelet setting the TaintExternalCloudProvider taint: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L266

The results in calling `initializeNode` function in cloud node-controller:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L323

This (in a healthy case) sends 4 GCE API calls to:
1. get node addresses: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L439 (as part of getNodeModifier call)
2. get instance type:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L452 (as part of getNodeModifiers call)
3. get instance:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L233 (as part of updateNodeAddresses call)
4. get node addresses (again):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L242 (as part of updateNodeAddresses call)

All those requests are read requests and could be replaced by a single call.
We could do that by introducing a simple struct like:
```
type InstanceMetadata struct {
  ProviderID ...
  Type ...
  NodeAddresses ...
}
```
and adding a method (or rather replacing the existing InstanceTypeByProviderID which is used only for this purpose) to Instances cloud-provider interface;
```
func InstanceMetadataByProviderID(...) (*InstanceMetadata, error)
```

With that change, we would be able to replace all that 4 calls with just a single API call.

This would be useful especially for creating large clusters (like 5k nodes), which may saturate the quota for API calls for quite some time.

This is quite significant size of refactoring, though it should be relatively mechanical task to do.

/sig cloud-provider
/sig scalability
/priority important-longterm

/help-wanted

Issue #3072: Support for repo URL with path is broken

Issue description:
When you have a repo URL with a path (e.g. `http://example.com/helm`) along with a chart URL (defined in `index.yaml`) which is relative (e.g. `charts/foo-1.2.3.tgz`), the resulting download URL is wrong: `http://example.com/helmchart/foo-1.2.3.tgz`.

This is due to the path concatenation logic in the `ResolveChartVersion` function, which has been altered by this commit:

https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/pull/2988/files

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Fix for relative chart path support in index.yaml
PR description:
This fixes a regression that I believe was added in version 2.7.0, with this particular commit:

https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/pull/2988/files

which breaks the case where your repo URL has a path suffix (e.g. `http://example.com/helm`, with possibly a trailing slash).. **and** your `index.yaml` file contains chart `urls` which are relative paths to it (instead of absolute URLs), which is actually the case with the [ChartMuseum](github.com/chartmuseum/chartmuseum). Before this commit, this particular use case _was_ supported, while it is not anymore.

This PR fixes #3072, and it also incidentally fixes #3057.

PR title: Tiller should only enforce what we expect from Helm
PR description:
https://github.com/kubernetes/helm/pull/3183 added a keepalive to the Helm client of 30s period, while Tiller was never configured to permit this, keeping the default minimum keepalive period of 5 minutes, disconnecting any clients which ping more regularly than this.

This commit enforces a minimum that is lower than what Helm is configured for, preventing these disconnections, and thus fixes #3409.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #6366: get script version check does not respect HELM_INSTALL_DIR

Issue description:
<!-- If you need help or think you have found a bug, please help us with your issue by entering the following information (otherwise you can delete this text): -->

When checking for the version of `helm` installed, the `get` script uses the `helm` binary on `PATH`. It should use the `helm` binary found in `HELM_INSTALL_DIR` instead

```
$ helm version
Client: &version.Version{SemVer:"v2.14.3", GitCommit:"0e7f3b6637f7af8fcfddb3d2941fcc7cbebb0085", GitTreeState:"clean"}

$ export HELM_INSTALL_DIR=/Users/cipriano/bin

$ $HELM_INSTALL_DIR/helm version
Client: &version.Version{SemVer:"v2.12.3", GitCommit:"eecf22f77df5f65c823aacd2dbd30ae6c65f186e", GitTreeState:"clean"}

$ ./get --version v2.14.3
Helm v2.14.3 is already v2.14.3
```

This is a bit of an edge case, where a user has `helm` installed and available on their `PATH`, but wants to install another version to a specific `HELM_INSTALL_DIR`. Currently it will take no action if the desired specified version to be installed is the same as the version available in `PATH`, regardless of what version is found at `HELM_INSTALL_DIR`. What it should do is check the version of `helm` using the binary located at `HELM_INSTALL_DIR` and update the version there if appropriate.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7377: Using the Helm SDK when no kubeconfig is available

Issue description:
Currently when using helm SDK, a `RESTClientGetter` is needed. This is trivial when a kubeconfig file is available. However when the program only have access to the CA, token/certs and url in memory, it becomes a bit more complicated.

In fact the program needs to implement the following interfaces:
- `ToRESTConfig() (*rest.Config, error)`
- `ToDiscoveryClient() (discovery.CachedDiscoveryInterface, error)`
- `ToRESTMapper() (meta.RESTMapper, error)`

Of course it can still be done with some magic, but then it is also needed to create a new abstraction over the namespace with the `ToRawKubeConfigLoader()` method.

A fix would be to add a `Namespace` field to the kube client in order to lighten a bit the custom implementation written to use Helm3 without a kubeconfig

PR title: fixed dependencies processing in case of helm install or upgrade for …
PR description:
fixes #7497
I have noticed that `helm install/upgrade` tries to resolve all dependencies. Issue #5184: Nested `null` values don't remove keys as expected

Issue description:
<https://github.com/helm/helm/pull/2648> allows for deletion of keys by setting `null` values in a `values.yaml` file. However it doesn't work for nested values, e.g.:

```yaml
web:
  livenessProbe:
    httpGet: null
    exec:
      command:
      - curl
      - -f
      - http://localhost:8080/api/v1/info

```

Ironically, above is a small variant on the example given in the docs, which I'm pretty sure does not actually do what it claims to: <https://docs.helm.sh/chart_template_guide/#deleting-a-default-key>

I suspect that since the template rendering doesn't seem to differentiate much between a null value and a value not being specified, that this warnings are being ignored and not having much effect.
