Issue #1990: Add lint rule for spec.matchLabels on Deployment

Issue description:
Resources like Deployment, ReplicaSet, and DaemonSet should, as a best practice, declare `selector.matchLabels` rules in their pod template:

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/tools/kubectl/object-management-using-declarative-config/#defining-controller-selectors-and-podtemplate-labels

Doing so prevents a number of odd-ball cases where pods are not appropriately updated.

We should write a linting rule to catch this case.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: feat: Detect missing selector during lint
PR description:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'closes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This issue closes #1990 by adding a quick test for `matchLabels` or `matchExpressions` in specific Kubernetes kinds. This was a requested feature because so many Helm issues were being filed because of malformed charts. I don't know if this is any longer necessary. If not, we can probably just close-won't-fix #1990.

Because a chart with no valid selector is _illegal_, this is an error. It catches `matchLabels` and `matchSelectors` (instead of just `selector`) because the requirement is that one of these two most be present. These are the fields frequently left off by chart authors.

Like all other chart lints, this does not enforce anything other than that the strings are present.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

This change will definitely cause some charts that did not pass before to fail a lint now. However, those charts would have been broken had they been installed.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1222: Manually kill containerd-shim when container is paused causes other docker command block forever

Issue description:
**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
Run the following script:
```bash
1     #!/bin/bash
2     i=0
3     while true; do
4             ((i++))
5             containerid=`docker run -tid ubuntu`
6             docker pause $containerid
7             kill -9 `docker top $containerid | awk 'NR==2{print $3}'`     # get shim pid of this container and kill it
8             docker top $containerid
9             echo "$i:success!"
10     done
```

**Describe the results you received:**
The script gets block within 10 seconds, it blocks at L8.

**Describe the results you expected:**
No block.

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**
After [containerd/containerd #1111](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/1111), kill shim of a paused container will first resume this container, then this container is killed. But when the the script blocks, I find the container is still paused. `handleSigkilledShim()` returns at https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/v0.2.x/runtime/process.go#L306, so the following `p.container.Resume()` is not reached.

That is to say, when `exit` pipe is closed since shim is killed, we can still see shim for a while. I have tried to add a sleep(10 milliseconds) before `e := unix.Kill(p.cmd.Process.Pid, 0)`, then the above script won't block for a long time.


@mlaventure @coolljt0725 Any ideas about this issue?

**Description**

containerd does have a stop function to [stop itself gracefully on `SIGTERM`](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/master/cmd/containerd/main_unix.go#L46).

However, there is no way to gracefully stop third party plugins.

CRI plugin does have [a stop function](https://github.com/containerd/cri-containerd/blob/master/pkg/server/service.go#L281). It stops containerd event monitor and the streaming server and possibly more components in the future.

Issue #4301: Slow Windows container start time when using servercore image

Issue description:
We are seeing slower launch times of Windows containers using servercore images (or images derived from servercore). Upon investigation, this appears to be due to the C:\Windows\System32\CatRoot directory modification timestamp being different from the value in the container. This causes the Windows catdb to be rebuilt on container launch, which impacts container startup time.

We have root caused this to an issue in the Windows layer unpack code in Microsoft/hcsshim. When unpacking a delta layer, the directory timestamps are not correctly reset to their proper values after removing files removed via whiteout. We are working on a fix, and will then need to revendor Microsoft/hcsshim. We are tracking the issue on the hcsshim side via https://github.com/microsoft/hcsshim/issues/830.

Note that this bug could have other impact as well, as in general it can cause delta layer directory timestamps to be incorrect. The primary impact we have observed is the slow start time with servercore container images.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1186: check PD list validation

Issue description:
pd1 is a standalone cluster(a), pd2 and pd3 is the other cluster(b). We have many TiKVs, when the TiKV bootstraps, it randomly selects a PD to connect, so we may have two TiKVs which have same store ID (1) but belong to different clusters (a and b). We use 1a and 1b to distinguish them.
When 1b is down and 1a restarts, it may connect to cluster b because it chooses the PD in PD list randomly. Badly, 1a can join the cluster b, can communicate with other TiKVs in the cluster b too and we will meet data corruption here.

When we start tikv with a pd list like `pd1:2379,pd2:2379,pd3:2379`, we must check these PDs are all in the same cluster. E,g, we can use `members` API to get all PD members. If we get pd1 and pd2 only in the response, we can think PD3 is not a valid PD. But here we should also consider the condition that PD3 has already been removed.

/cc @huachaohuang

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: pd: validate PD list
PR description:
`validate_pd_list` only accepts PD endpoints that are in the same PD cluster. It treats a removed PD as an invalied PD node. ~~It only validates once at the beginning of raftkv startup.~~ It validates the list every time when the tikv trys to connect a PD.

---

Let's say there are two PD clusters, one consists three nodes, and the other is a standlone node. Details:

```
cluster-id: 1
pd1 client urls: "127.0.0.1:12379"
pd2 client urls: "127.0.0.1:22379"
pd3 client urls: "127.0.0.1:32379"
```

```
cluster-id: 1
pd1 client urls: "127.0.0.1:42379"
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4389: Try to remove codegen from tikv-server, etc.

Issue description:
During my profiling I've noticed that the codegen for tikv-server takes almost as long as the codegen for the tikv lib. Codegen being the time it takes for rustc to emit llvm IR.

This is surprising since the tikv-server binary contains very little code.

My guess is there's a ton of generics instantiation in the crate, which would be duplicated in the other bins as well, and maybe in the lib.

Move as much code as reasonable directly into the library and see if that has any effect on the codegen time in tikv-server, and any effect on the overall build time.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Moving code from bin/util into tikv, and crate docs
PR description:
## What have you changed? (mandatory)

This moves most of the `src/bin/util` code and most of `src/bin/tikv-server.rs` into the `tikv` library. In addition to making it easier to use the library to create a tikv server, it also reduces the amount of utility coded that is recompiled between the three binaries.

This is a follow up to my [previous cleanup pr](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/pull/4513). It does a number of things.

It started out as a documentation patch, and I add some basic crate docs. Then I started documenting some of the configuration methods, but found I wanted more of the setup code from tikv-server, so that it would be easier to write examples.

So then I pulled in some commits for https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/4389, moving all of `src/bin/util` into the `tikv` library, and then the setup code from tikv-server. Now it should be easy to show documentation examples for the API.

Moving code from the bins into tikv will reduce the amount of compilation work, but won't reduce serial compilation time.

It is getting pretty big, so I hope to land it before continuing.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #6366: Two overlapped snapshot may be applied together which may cause panic or loss of data

Issue description:
Theoretically, the pending_snapshot_region and region_ranges in StoreMeta should prevent overlapped snapshots.
But it is problematic sometimes.

At each end of raftstore's batch, the received snapshot region ids in this batch are removed from pending_snapshot_regions.
Most of the time, this removed region will be updated to region_ranges, so it can still prevent overlapped snapshots.

However, a pending snapshot may not be handled for some reason. e.g. waiting for its source region to destroy.
In this case, this snapshot's region range is larger than the original range and is not updated to region_ranges.

After its source region is destroyed, another overlapped snapshot B is received. (overlap with its source region and maybe from a new peer)
Two overlapped snapshot will be applied together and break the data in this range.
It may cause some serious problems. e.g. panic, loss of data.

The simple fix method is just remove handled snapshot region id not all received snapshot region id in this batch.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: raftstore: make destroy overlapped regions and apply snapshot atomically
PR description:
Signed-off-by: Liqi Geng <gengliqiii@gmail.com>


###  What have you changed?

The operation of destroying overlapped regions and applying snapshot must be atomic, otherwise, it may cause a target peer can't find its corresponding source peer when applying `CommitMerge` log in extreme cases.

A tikv may crash after a target peer does not become `Applying` state which means it will not apply snapshot after this tikv restarts. But its corresponding source peers may have destroyed.
After this tikv restarts, a new leader may send logs to this target peer in some cases.
Then the panic will happen because it can not find its source peers when applying `CommitMerge` log.

In addition to the above problem, this PR also fix https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/6366 and https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/7002.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7364: Txn: collapsing the rollback record of pessimistic lock could cause inconsistency

Issue description:
## Bug Report

### What version of TiKV are you using?

master

### What did happened?

A false assertion is found in: https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/c3f9fba14b04811e77614bcd50007bad17e251c3/src/storage/mvcc/txn.rs#L684-L691

where pessimistic transactions may commit successfully even when some of its keys it prewrited are rollbacked by cleanup-resolve procedural invoked by a duplicated cleanup command, which is sent before for cleaning up the pessimistic lock.

### Steps to reproduce

Assume that we have three clients {c1, c2, c3} and two keys {k1, k2}:

1. Pessimistic client c1 acquires a pessimistic lock on k1(primary), k2. But the command for k1 is lost at this point.
2. Optimistic client c2 requires to clean up the lock on k2
3. k1 is rollbacked and a write record `("rollback", c1_start_ts, not_protected)` is written into k1 (not_protected because the lock on k1 is missing), and a `resolve(primary=k1, ts=c1_start_ts)`(*1) is sent but lost at this point.
4. Client c3 prewrites k1
5. Client c2 requires to clean up the lock on k1
6. k1 is rollbacked and the rollback write record is **collapsed** to `("rollback", c3_start_ts, protected/not_protected)`
7. Client c1 retries to lock on k1
8. k1 is locked by c1
9. Client c1 prewrites k1, k2
10. k1, k2 are prewrited by c1, and c1 received the prewrite succeed response
11. The lost resolve command (*1) in step 3 is received by k2, therefore k2 is rollbacked
12. Client c1 commit k1
13. k1 is committed, while k2 is rollbacked

Then atomic guarantee is broken.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: txn: write protected rollback when cleanup with missing lock
PR description:
Signed-off-by: Dian Luo <andylokandy@hotmail.com>

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #7484: The unified read pool should not use start_ts as task id

Issue description:
## Bug Report

### What version of TiKV are you using?

4.0-beta.2 and up

### What operating system and CPU are you using?

Unrelated

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a transaction, run a big query (for example `SELECT COUNT(*)` from a big table).
2. Start some other big queries.
3. While those big queries are in process, run a small query (for example a point select) in the transaction started in 1.

### What did you expect?

The small query finishes quickly.

### What did happened?

Because we use start_ts as the task id, the priority of the small query is lowered by the previously executed big query, thus it may take some time to finish. I don't think it's a reasonable strategy.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: *: use given task id or random number as task id
PR description:
- [x] Depends on https://github.com/pingcap/kvproto/pull/604

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: Closes #7484

Problem Summary:

It's not suitable in all cases to use start ts as the task id for the unified read pool. For example, in the same transaction, a big query is executed and the following point selects are also downgraded.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

https://github.com/pingcap/kvproto/pull/604 adds `task_id` to kv context. We can use it to generate a better task id instead of using start_ts in coprocessor.
Task id tends to be generated in serial. The algorithm is replacing the high 16 bits of start ts (which is not so representative) with the low 16-bits of the given task id.
This PR also changes to let all storage tasks use random number as task id. These tasks tend to end fast so we don't bother to give them a meaningful task id. (Maybe we can do it in the future)

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

Allow using the task ID provided by the client as the identifier used by the unified read pool to avoid unexpected priority lowered by another task in the same transaction .

PR description:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiKV!

If you haven't already, please read TiKV's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.

If you're unsure about anything, just ask; somebody should be along to answer within a day or two.

PR Title Format:
1. module [, module2, module3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed
-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #7375, close #7850, close #7880, close tidb-challenge-program/bug-hunting-issue#72

Problem Summary:

The backup/restore did not have timeout and retry. This causes a single spurious network error to either catastrophically kill the entire BR task or block the BR thread pool forever.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

1. ("Restore" supports retrying externally through pingcap/br#298, so for now we're not going to implement retry for "Restore").
2. The "Backup" gRPC produces a stream, which cannot be retried externally. Therefore, we implemented retry directly in the backup service (`ExternalStorage::write` in particular) to fix #7850.
3. The produced backup file can have size up to 135 MiB. This is not a good idea to retry the upload entirely. So we implemented [Multipart Upload](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/mpuoverview.html) on S3. Unfortunately `tame-gcs` does not support resumable upload EmbarkStudios/tame-gcs#24 so this won't work for GCS. (This also fix #7375.)
    * Unfortunately, we need to copy the SST file into memory and clone several times in order to retry.
4. We have also replaced `reqwest` by `hyper` so those `convert_request` and `convert_response` are no longer needed.
5. For "Restore", we added a timeout around `ExternalStorage::read`, so that a stuck download won't block the thread pool forever, to fix #7880.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
    * Backup and restore against a `minio` S3 storage.

Side effects

- Performance regression
    - Consumes more MEM: Backup may need to copy the entire SST file several times.
    - Multi-part upload and retrying would produce many more requests per file.

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

* Improved robustness of backup and restore for S3 and GCS storage.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: backup,config: set backup thread pool size via config instead of gRPC (#8193)
PR description:
cherry-pick #8193 to release-4.0

---

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close pingcap/br#394, close #8076.

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

This is the companion PR of pingcap/br#396.

In #5553, the `backup` component gained ability to an adjustable thread pool size. The size is provided via the incoming gRPC request. Given [how the ThreadPool is implemented in TiKV](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/b45e052df8fb5d66aa8b3a77b5c992ddbfbb79df/components/tikv_util/src/threadpool.rs#L204-L219), a user can easily (accidentally) DoS all TiKV servers by setting the thread pool size to a huge number like 2<sup>32</sup>-1.

Furthermore, when we provide the thread pool size through gRPC, the backup client (BR) must determine the suitable concurrency number in some ad-hoc way.

This PR solves both issue by moving the thread pool size back as a TiKV config:

```toml
[backup]
num-threads = 24
```

The default value is set to (0.75 × Number of CPUs) to better utilize the available resources. The value can still be dynamically configured, but given this more practical default value it should be much less needed.

### Related changes

- PR to update `pingcap/docs`/`pingcap/docs-cn`:
- PR to update `pingcap/tidb-ansible`:

- Unit test

messages.content: A repository contains the following reported issue: Issue #8486: Too many rocksdb tombstone may slow batch-get Issue description: In the case, there are a lot of deletes for a range on the transaction level. Once GCed, it leads to a lot of tombstone marks in rocksdb. It is invisible, but iterating on them does have the same overhead as iterating on visible keys. So when batch-get on the GCed keys, it calls `writecf.seek(key)` for each key and needs to iterate over a lot of tombstones for every key internally which hurts performance greatly. Also, coprocessor may suffer the same issue. Some possible solution: - use `prefix_seek` and `prefix_same_as_start` - set `max-skippable-internal-keys=1` for `writecf.seek(key + ts)`. If it encounters a tombstone, it is enough to ensure the key is deleted at this version(without collapse rollback). So it can abort the seek directly, instead of seeking the next visible key. - sort the keys of batch-get, and`PointGetter` records the key of the last `writecf.seek()`. If the recorded_key > now_key then now_key must be deleted. So it won't seek the range with lots of tombstones again and again. - Use rocksdb single delete to relieve(Can't solve it completely) A pull request was created to resolve it: PR title: storage: Optimize seek write for many tombstones PR description: ### What problem does this PR solve? optimize seek write when there are too many tombstones. A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #8229: MvccTxn can't make use of near_seek

Issue description:
## Bug Report

`MvccTxn` always uses `seek` to find write records. The reason is `MvccReader` in it always creates a new write cursor:
https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/11cbf057ba8dec3a0833a9948b5ae9ec54d6113d/src/storage/mvcc/reader/reader.rs#L129-L145

It's better to use `next` to get older versions in some cases. For example, in https://github.com/tikv/tikv/issues/7024, you can see 578k seeks per second. Please be careful with prefix seek in rocksdb, it can't guarantee a total order of all keys, but only keys for the same prefix.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: txn: make use of near_seek for write-cf
PR description:
Signed-off-by: youjiali1995 <zlwgx1023@gmail.com>

<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiKV!

If you haven't already, please read TiKV's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.

If you're unsure about anything, just ask; somebody should be along to answer within a day or two.

PR Title Format:
1. module [, module2, module3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed
-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #8229  <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

`MvccTxn` doesn't make use of `near_seek`. It creates a write cursor for every seek which may cost a lot if many versions exist.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

Add a single key mode for `MvccReader` which uses a single write cursor for each user key. When the current key is changed, a new write cursor is created to guarantee the total order of all keys due to prefix seek. This check involves a key comparison for every seek, but the cost is in a single-digit nanosecond.

### Related changes

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #12827: Fix negative repo ID in artifact table if the repo exists in repository table

Issue description:
In 1.x -> 2.0 migration the repo id of an artifact may be set to negative:

```
/*set the media type*/
UPDATE artifact AS art
    SET type='IMAGE', repository_id=repo.repository_id,
    manifest_media_type=blob.content_type,
    media_type=(
    CASE
        /*v2 manifest*/
        WHEN blob.content_type='application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' THEN
            'application/vnd.docker.container.image.v1+json'
        /*manifest list*/
        WHEN blob.content_type='application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json' THEN
            'application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json'
        /*v1 manifest*/
        ELSE
            'application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v1+prettyjws'
    END
    )
    FROM repository AS repo, blob AS blob
    WHERE art.repo=repo.name AND art.digest=blob.digest;
/*
It's a workaround for issue https://github.com/goharbor/harbor/issues/11754
The phenomenon is the repository data is gone, but artifacts belong to the repository are still there.
To set the repository_id to a negative, and cannot duplicate.
*/
UPDATE artifact SET repository_id = 0-artifact.id, type='IMAGE', media_type='UNKNOWN', manifest_media_type='UNKNOWN' WHERE repository_id IS NULL;
```

This assume the `repository_id IS NULL`  only happens when there's no corresponding record in the repository table, however, it may also happen when there are inconsistencies between blob table and artifact table.

We should reset the "repo_id" of these records to positive if the repository with the same name exist in repository table.

PR title: middleware/secondary: fix crash with no zone
PR description:
When CoreDNS starts up and can't get a zone transfer going the Apex is
empty. This `nil` is then transformed into wireformat, which fails with
a nil pointer dereference in Go DNS.

In this case we should just return SERVFAIL, because we don't have any
info (yet). Note the lookup code returned NXDOMAIN, which is correct
from a lookup standpoint, but also invalidates every name in the future
loaded zone.

Anyway, look for an apex before doing the lookup and return SERVFAIL if
nothing is found.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1678: plugin/forward: make read timeout configurable

Issue description:
The recently added dynamic timeout feature (#1659) may give worse results than fixed timeout under some circumstances, e.g. at high load when upstream servers are overloaded. Dynamic timeout allows us re-sending unanswered queries faster, and this could be a problem, because we make upstream server load even higher.

In my tests I saw RTT (round trip time) as minimal as 10μs. For comparison, transmission of 50 bytes (400 bits) over 100Mbit network takes about 4μs. So, we can easily catch timeout at the moment when message was partially read which results in truncated messages

Therefore, I propose to introduce minimal timeout. The reason why we added dynamic timeout feature is to have more attempts to re-send query (probably to different upstreams) during limited period (5 seconds).  Even if we set minimal timeout to 200ms we will get around 25 attempts which is quite enough. No sense to retry faster and create additional server load.

I propose to add a timeout option to forward plugin like below
```
forward .:53 {
    timeout MAX MIN RATIO WEIGHT
}

```
If user specifies only the first parameter (**MAX**) then dynamic timeout will not be used

**MAX** - maximum read timeout which is currently defined by constant `timeout `
https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/e671e22e657b2fcb1580abd311e9c340b20b9e96/plugin/forward/proxy.go#L93

**MIN** - minimum read timeout. Timeout is based on average RTT but cannot be less than MIN
**RATIO** - desired timeout/RTT ratio. I.e. timeout will be calculated as (average  RTT) * RATIO
**WEIGHT** - defines how much average RTT is influenced by current RTT, i.e. avgRTT = avgRTT + (newRTT-avgRTT)/WEIGHT like in function below
https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/e671e22e657b2fcb1580abd311e9c340b20b9e96/plugin/forward/connect.go#L27-L30

A pull request was created to resolve it:

Issue #661: Add GetSamplingStrategy handler to collector

Issue description:
The agent proxies all sampling requests to collector, but there is no handler there :-(

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Add sampling handler and sampling strategy store
PR description:
This adds a tchannel sampling handler and a static sampling strategy store that reads sampling strategies from a json file.

Issue #1578: [jaeger-query] Leading zeros stripped from trace IDs

Issue description:
<!--
Welcome to the Jaeger project! 👋🎉

- Please search for existing issues to avoid creating duplicate bugs/feature requests.

    - the forum https://groups.google.com/d/forum/jaeger-tracing
    (but please don't double post)
-->

## Requirement - what kind of business use case are you trying to solve?

I would like to view traces in Jaeger UI where the trace ID has leading 0s.

## Problem - what in Jaeger blocks you from solving the requirement?

When jaeger-query returns data for traces where there are leading 0s in the trace ID, the leading 0s are stripped from the trace ID, within the data. E.g. for a trace with ID `0123`, all of the spans returned refer to trace ID `123`.

For each trace returned by jaeger-query, this applies to:

* The trace ID on the root of the trace data object
* The trace ID fields in each span
* The trace ID fields in internal references

## Proposal - what do you suggest to solve the problem or improve the existing situation?

The zeros should not be stripped.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Do not remove leading zeros in trace ID hex string
PR description:
Resolves #1578 and probably #1951

## Motivation

Among randomly generated and uniformly distributed trace IDs, only 1/16th of them start with 0 followed by a significant digit, 1/256th start with two 0s, and so on in decreasing geometric progression. Therefore, trimming the leading 0s is a very modest optimization on the size of the data being transmitted or stored.

However, trimming 0s leads to ambiguities when the IDs are used as correlations with other monitoring systems, such as logging, that treat the IDs as opaque strings and cannot establish the equivalence between padded and unpadded IDs. It is also incompatible with W3C Trace Context and Zipkin B3 format, both of which include all leading 0s, so an application instrumented with OpenTelemetry SDKs may be logging different trace ID strings than application instrumented with Jaeger SDKs (related issue #1657).

Open question: this change may prevent ES backend from reading the old traces if their IDs had leading zeroes, because previously the zeroes were not added to string representation, and now they are. Roughly one in 16 traces will be affected.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2037: Expose Samara Kafka producer/consumer configurations to command line.

Issue description:
## Requirement - what kind of business use case are you trying to solve?

We are using Jaeger with Ingester.  On Collector, we are setting SPAN_STORAGE_TYPE=kafka.  We would like to tune Kafka configurations for performance.  The default Kafka Samara config is resulting in over 150% CPU usage on Kafka broker for just 40k spans per minute.

## Problem - what in Jaeger blocks you from solving the requirement?
Jaeger provided these producer settings
```
      --kafka.producer.authentication string          Authentication type used to authenticate with kafka cluster. e.g. none, kerberos, tls (default "none")
      --kafka.producer.brokers string                 The comma-separated list of kafka brokers. i.e. '127.0.0.1:9092,0.0.0:1234' (default "127.0.0.1:9092")
      --kafka.producer.compression string             (experimental) Type of compression (none, gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd) to use on messages (default "none")
      --kafka.producer.compression-level int          (experimental) compression level to use on messages. gzip = 1-9 (default = 6), snappy = none, lz4 = 1-17 (default = 9), zstd = -131072 - 22 (default = 3)
      --kafka.producer.encoding string                Encoding of spans ("json" or "protobuf") sent to kafka. (default "protobuf")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.config-file string    Path to Kerberos configuration. i.e /etc/krb5.conf (default "/etc/krb5.conf")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.keytab-file string    Path to keytab file. i.e /etc/security/kafka.keytab (default "/etc/security/kafka.keytab")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.password string       The Kerberos password used for authenticate with KDC
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.realm string          Kerberos realm
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.service-name string   Kerberos service name (default "kafka")
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.use-keytab            Use of keytab instead of password, if this is true, keytab file will be used instead of password
      --kafka.producer.kerberos.username string       The Kerberos username used for authenticate with KDC
      --kafka.producer.protocol-version string        Kafka protocol version - must be supported by kafka server
      --kafka.producer.required-acks string           (experimental) Required kafka broker acknowledgement. i.e. noack, local, all (default "local")
      --kafka.producer.tls.ca string                  Path to the TLS CA for the Kafka connection
      --kafka.producer.tls.cert string                Path to the TLS Certificate for the Kafka connection
      --kafka.producer.tls.key string                 Path to the TLS Key for the Kafka connection
      --kafka.producer.topic string
```
Setting `--kafka.producer.required-acks` to `noack` helps a little, reducing CPU usage on Kafka broker by 8%.  We experimented setting github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pkg/kafka/producer/config.go with the following parameters.  It resulted in 10 times improvement in Kafka broker CPU usage.
```
        saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Bytes = 128000
        saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Frequency = time.Duration(1 * time.Second)
```

## Proposal - what do you suggest to solve the problem or improve the existing situation?
At a minimum, Jaeger should expose the above 2 settings to the command line.  Ideally Jaeger should expose all producer/consumer configurations.
Given that each Kafka client has it's own naming for configurations.  I would suggest Jaeger use Kafka's official parameter names for it's client.  For example, `saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Bytes` should be exposed as `batch.size` and `saramaConfig.Producer.Flush.Frequency` should be exposed as `linger.ms`
<!-- It's ok if you don't have one. -->

## Any open questions to address

<!-- Questions that should be answered before proceeding with implementation. -->

PR title: Add CLI flags for Kafka batching params
PR description:
Resolves #2037
The default Samara Kafka client writes to Kafka broker for every single span received.
This is not efficient and caused high CPU utilization on the brokers as well as high network traffic.
Samara Kafka client has options to enable batching.  These options needed to be exposed
to the command for performance tuning. The option names matches official Kafka documentation and
not specific to Samara.

PR title: Mons started as a replicaset instead of directly as a pod
PR description:
One replicaset is created for each mon, with a replica count of 1. The mons are assigned to a node, which is critical for recovery of the mon. When a new pod is started, the same metadata dir will be available on the same node as long as a hostDir was specified. If no hostDir was specified then quorum is required to restore that monitor. Bringing up a new mon to replace a bad pod is dependent on #586. A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1701: Flex driver conflicts when multiple rook system namespaces are running

Issue description:
When there are multiple rook namespaces running, we observe that the flex volume drivers for the namespaces will conflict.
- The agent pods will be watching the same unix socket
- If one namespace is terminated, the unix socket will be deleted from under the agent in the other namespace

The latter is an issue commonly in the integration tests running in jenkins. Immediately after one test suite is removed, another suite starts. The removal might actually take several seconds to complete and will remove the socket from under the new namespace.

To allow multiple namespaces to use the flex driver, we will need to base the name of the flex driver on the namespace where the operator/agent pair are running. Since the drivers would be registered under rook.io, we wouldn't have to worry about conflicting with any other driver.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Base flex driver name on the namespace
PR description:
Signed-off-by: travisn <tnielsen@redhat.com>

<!-- Please take a look at our [Contributing](https://rook.io/docs/rook/master/development-flow.html)
documentation before submitting a Pull Request!
Thank you for contributing to Rook! -->

Multiple rook system namespaces cannot be currently run because of the conflict between using the same flex driver. This change creates a driver name based on the namespace to avoid that conflict. For backward compatibility, the agent will also watch the unix socket for the old driver name (rook).

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1389: Improve Rook's Security Model

Issue description:
Rook currently uses multiple namespaces and service accounts. The rook operator can create and delete namespaces, service accounts, roles and role bindings on the fly. As a result rook requires a *very* privileged service account (see [here](https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/cluster/examples/kubernetes/rook-operator.yaml#L9)).

For production clusters this not going to work. We need to explore running in a mode where we do not have privileges to destroy the entire cluster. Also creating a deleting namespace is not necessarily something that every cluster-admin is going to want us to do.

If a cluster-admin wants to set policies (PSP, SCC, resource quotas, etc.) they need to be able to control which service accounts and namespaces Rook uses. Creating namespaces and service accounts on the fly means that these policies would need to be dynamically applied too.

This is a complicated issue but it's one that we should front load. Its come up in the following places #1314 #1337 #1348 #1211 and possible more. Also discussion on twitter here: https://twitter.com/the_sttts/status/945077544587616257

 I'm going to write a design doc and link it here when its ready.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Refactor cluster roles for minimal rbac access
PR description:
Signed-off-by: travisn <tnielsen@redhat.com>

Description of your changes:
Per the [security model](https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/design/security-model.md#proposed-changes) proposal:
- There is one serviceAccount per namespace, one for `rook-system` and one for each cluster that is created: `rook-ceph-cluster`.
- The operator, agent, and discovery daemons all run with the `rook-system` service account
- The OSD daemon runs with the `rook-ceph-cluster` service account. Other cluster daemons (mon, mgr, mds, rgw) run with the default service account since they do not require access to k8s resources.
- Rook no longer creates service accounts, cluster roles, roles, etc. These must be created by the admin.

Differing from the security model spec, a ClusterRoleBinding was needed for several resources:
- Rook CRDs: Watched and handled across all namespaces
- Pods: The agent needs to analyze pods for fencing
- PVs & PVCs: The operator provisioner needs to create, delete, list, etc
- Nodes: Used to determine on which nodes to place mons
- Storage classes: watched by the operator

The `rook-ceph-core` role was created for the namespace-specific resources and the `rook-ceph-global` role was created for cluster-wide resources.

Which issue is resolved by this Pull Request:
Resolves #1389

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1752: Ceph daemon names should match k8s pod names where possible

Issue description:
To make it easier to troubleshoot the Ceph daemons, the pod names should match the daemon names wherever possible.

### Stateless daemons

#### MDS
The name of the mds will be the same as the pod name. MDS is stateless therefore maintaining a consistent name is not needed.

Currently the mds daemon name only consists of the random k8s pod suffix such as `fn72k`, which means now we would use more of the pod name. If the pod name is `rook-ceph-mds-myfs-5f8556bd99-fn72k`, the daemon would be `mds.myfs-5f8556bd99-fn72k`.

#### RGW
Clients need to know the service name rather than the pod name. The rgw service will start with the service name for the `rgw_zone` and `rgw_zonegroup` settings. Need to investigate if the daemon name is exposed in the service map.

#### Mgr
There is only one mgr in Rook named `rook-ceph-mgr`. The mgr name needs to match the service name rather than the pod name. The service name is constant so that clients can connect to the dashboard and prometheus metrics. There is no need for multiple mgrs since Kubernetes will failover the pod automatically. The name is currently `rook-ceph-mgr0` so we can remove the `0` suffix.

The pod can be queried with a label:
```
kubectl -n rook-ceph get pod -l app=rook-ceph-mgr
```

### Mons and OSDs

#1656 will name the osds to match the OSD IDs and #1751 will take care of renaming the mons to follow this pattern. However, the mon and osd pod names will still have a random k8s suffix in addition to the daemon name. For example, the daemon name and deployment name for a mon would be `rook-ceph-mon-a`, while its pod name might be `rook-ceph-mon-a-5f8556bd99-gjpd8`.

The recommended way to work with the mon and osd pods will to be use labels. This example shows how a specific mon or osd pod might be queried.
```
kubectl -n rook-ceph get pod -l mon=rook-ceph-mon-a
```

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Name mgr and mds pods more consistently
PR description:
<!-- Please take a look at our [Contributing](https://rook.io/docs/rook/master/development-flow.html)
documentation before submitting a Pull Request!
Thank you for contributing to Rook! -->

The naming of the deployments and pods will now be more correlated with the ceph daemon names when troubleshooting the ceph cluster.
- The name of the mgr is now `rook-ceph-mgr` instead of `rook-ceph-mgr0`. There is only ever one of them.
- The name of the mds daemon is now the entire suffix of the pod instead of just the last suffix. For example, if the pod name is `rook-ceph-mds-myfs-7b9c79f684-h7dqj`, the mds daemon name would be `myfs-7b9c79f684-h7dqj` as seen in `ceph -s`, instead of `h7dqj`.

Issue #2021: "rbd map" hangs in toolbox

Issue description:
As stated in the [docs](https://rook.io/docs/rook/v0.8/direct-tools.html), `rbd map` hangs (while still succeeding) when running it in the toolbox:
```sh
# Map the rbd device. If this command appears to hang, ctrl-c and check if it actually completed successfully by continuing.
rbd map replicapool/test
```

Because I was a bit annoyed by this, I decided to look into it. With a bit of help from #ceph-devel on IRC, I found that, after mapping the block image, "rbd map" [waits for an udev add event](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/master/src/krbd.cc#L182-L251) for the /dev/rbd*X* block device. Using `udev monitor` inside the toolbox I noticed it didn't receive those events (while `udev monitor` on the host was receiving them). Googling around, I [found out](https://dummdida.tumblr.com/post/121087781445/re-udev-events-in-a-container) that the only way to get a container to receive udev events is to run the container with `--net=host`. Changing https://github.com/rook/rook/blame/master/Documentation/toolbox.md#L47 to `hostNetwork: true` fixed the hanging issue.

So, my suggestion is to change `hostNetwork: true` in the toolbox documentation (maybe with a comment that setting it to `false` will make `rbd map` hang), and refine the already existing hang comment. If you agree, I can create a PR.

The [master build](https://jenkins.rook.io/blue/organizations/jenkins/rook%2Frook/detail/master/764/pipeline) failed due to a crd existing from a previous test. The test attempts to delete the crd, remove the finalizer from the crd, and try again. ```

```

The test needs to ensure all the resources (service accounts, roles, etc) are properly created before continuing with the test.

**Expected behavior:**
Successful build

**Environment**:
Jenkins

documentation before submitting a Pull Request!

PR title: Publish the build independent from the integration test results
PR description:
Signed-off-by: travisn <tnielsen@redhat.com>

<!-- Please take a look at our [Contributing](https://rook.io/docs/rook/master/development-flow.html)
documentation before submitting a Pull Request!
Thank you for contributing to Rook! -->

**Description of your changes:**
This change will cause master and release builds to be published before the integration tests are run. There are some positive and negative aspects to this:

PROS:
- Published builds match what has been merged
- Random integration test failures don't block the publishing of the build

CONS:
- If there is a significant failure shown by the integration tests, the build will be published anyway

I wouldn't be surprised if there is much debate around this, but the reality of the situation is that the random failures in integration tests are too painful not to do this. It doesn't mean we deprioritize fixing the integration test issues, but this will help us ensure our published images match what has been merged to the repo. I'm not worried about the integration tests finding significant issues after the merge, because they would have already been vetted **before** the merge.

As an example, we haven't had a successful master build for 6 days, but there was a breaking change three days ago that requires a new build. See #2329.

Issue description:
<!-- **Are you in the right place?**
1. For issues or feature requests, please create an issue in this repository.
2. For general technical and non-technical questions, we are happy to help you on our [Rook.io Slack](https://Rook-io.slack.com).
3. Did you already search the existing open issues for anything similar? -->

**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Feature Request

**What should the feature do:**

For performance vs. availability tradeoffs, EdgeFS allows flexible selection of sync operation. We need to provide a way to change it via cluster CRD. Example:

```yaml
...
  storage:
    config:
      sync: 3
...
```

This has to be cluster  or node scope option. Default is 1, i.e. consistent in case of software crash or power loss.

**What is use case behind this feature:**

To allow users flexibility they need during deployment. If they need absolutely durable storage, sync has to be set to 3. If they want consistency with reduced durability, it can be 2 or 1. If they need scratch-pad performance, sync can be set to 0.

Issue #3204: rook-ceph-mgr: Prometheus-Annotations in wrong place

Issue description:
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**
Default Configuration puts prometheus annotations at the deployment-leve of the rook-ceph-mgr pod, which won't get picked up by "default" prometheus-config.

```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  annotations:
    ...
    prometheus.io/port: "9283"
    prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
...
```

**Expected behavior:**
Annotation should be either in the pod-template or at the service-level for prometheus to scrape all the pods or only the service.

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**
- deploy prometheus with example-config from https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/master/documentation/examples/prometheus- kubernetes.yml
- deploy default rook-v1.0.1
- prometheus wont scrape rook-ceph-mgr

**Environment**:
* Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare-metal
* Rook version (use `rook version` inside of a Rook Pod): v1.0.1
* Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.13.5
* Kubernetes cluster type (e.g. Tectonic, GKE, OpenShift): Rancher2
* Storage backend status (e.g. for Ceph use `ceph health` in the [Rook Ceph toolbox](https://rook.io/docs/rook/master/ceph-toolbox.html)): HEALTH_OK

regards,
Roman

Issue #3448: WAL and DB optimization

Issue description:
**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Feature Request
Today I updated to Nautilus, and now every OSD is complaining:

`osd.32 spilled over 11 GiB metadata from 'db' device (1.9 GiB used of 20 GiB) to slow device`

I found this thread:

http://lists.ceph.com/pipermail/ceph-users-ceph.com/2019-February/033286.html

```
Bluestore/RocksDB will only put the next level up size of DB on flash if the whole size will fit.
These sizes are roughly 3GB,30GB,300GB. Anything in-between those sizes are pointless. Only ~3GB of SSD will ever be used out of a
28GB partition.
```

Rook by default creates a 20GB partitions, from which only 3 are actually used (not sure about the newer scheme, probably the same?)

I have the cluster with 1.7PB total, 700 TB used, installed long ago, so it has an old scheme with symlinks to partitions, and it would be really hard to delete and recreate the nodes to have the new scheme of WAL.

**What should the feature do:**
Would it be possible to migrate to the new scheme without deleting the current data? Also I'd like to use the https://github.com/rook/rook/pull/3213 to spread the WALs to several NVME's, again without the need to delete the whole node (those have 8*12 TB drives each, and take forever to backfill)

**What is use case behind this feature:**
Above

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #3810: Dashboard port / service very missleading

Issue description:
**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**

Ceph dashboard should work out of the box even with https disabled.

**Expected behavior:**

A few manual tweaks are required.

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**

As hinted in [this issue](https://github.com/rook/rook/issues/2809#issuecomment-472666545) the [config code](https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/pkg/operator/ceph/cluster/mgr/config.go#L46-L53) for the port still looks like this:
```
func (c *Cluster) dashboardPort() int {
	if c.dashboard.Port == 0 {
		// select default port
		return dashboardPortHTTPS
	}
	// crd validates port >= 0
	return c.dashboard.Port
}
```

This sets the default port to `dashboardPortHTTPS`, no matter if `c.dashboard.SSL` is enabled or not.

Please default to `dashboardPortHTTP` if `c.dashboard.SSL` is disabled.

----

Furthermore the [Code](https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/pkg/operator/ceph/cluster/mgr/spec.go#L323) will always create a port `https-dashboard` even if no https is involved.

This is not only very misleading, but also makes ingress controllers like [traefik](https://docs.traefik.io/configuration/backends/kubernetes/#tls-communication-between-traefik-and-backend-pods) assume communication using https. (And therefore breaks the ingress.)

Please only prefix `https` if `c.dashboard.SSL` is enabled.

**Environment**:
* OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Container Linux
* Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare metal
* Rook version (use `rook version` inside of a Rook Pod): v1.0.6 / master
* Storage backend version (e.g. for ceph do `ceph -v`): 13.2.2
* Kubernetes cluster type (e.g. Tectonic, GKE, OpenShift): typhoon

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Ceph: Use HTTP port if SSL is disabled
PR description:
**Description of your changes:**

Using port 8443 / dashboardHTTPS when not running HTTPS
is confusing, so use the dashboardHTTP port (7000 by
default) instead.

Also don't expose the dashboard port as "https-dashboard"
when not using https, instead expose as "dashboard".

**Which issue is resolved by this Pull Request:**

Issue #3912: Finalizer should not check for flex volumes if flex is disabled

Issue description:
<!-- **Are you in the right place?**
1. For issues or feature requests, please create an issue in this repository.
2. For general technical and non-technical questions, we are happy to help you on our [Rook.io Slack](https://slack.rook.io/).
3. Did you already search the existing open issues for anything similar? -->

**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**
The CephCluster currently has a finalizer that will prevent the cluster from being deleted until the volumes are cleaned up. This is necessary to abort the deletion if there are any volumeAttachments. Otherwise, the volumes would hang and never be able to detach.

If the flex driver is disabled and there is no volumeAttached CRD even defined, the operator will hit this error and the finalizer will never be removed:
```
 2019-09-03 09:52:25.883690 I | op-cluster: cluster openshift-storage has a deletion timestamp
2019-09-03 09:52:25.884772 E | op-cluster: failed finalizer for cluster. failed to get volume attachments for operator namespace openshift-storage: the server could not find the requested resource (get volumes.rook.io)
```

The operator should ignore that error and remove the finalizer in that case.


**Expected behavior:**
The finalizer to be removed if there is no volumeAttachment CRD defined.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Backport: Ceph: Remove finalizer even if flex is disabled
PR description:
When the flex driver is disabled, the check for
volume attachments will fail and the finalizer
is never removed. To avoid this, just log the
failure to list volumes and remove the
finalizer anyway.

Resolves #3912

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4633: Ceph operator: devicesInUse should be set to false when initialization fail

Issue description:
<!-- **Are you in the right place?**
1. For issues or feature requests, please create an issue in this repository.
2. For general technical and non-technical questions, we are happy to help you on our [Rook.io Slack](https://slack.rook.io/).
3. Did you already search the existing open issues for anything similar? -->

**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**
When initialization of cluster failed, `devicesInUse` variable can be set to `true` (if `spec.storage.useAllDevices` is set to true)  and then, when we update `CephCluster` k8s manifest (to get initialization to work), `devicesInUse` is already set to `true` and "using all devices in more than one namespace is not supported" error can happen.

**Expected behavior:**

When initialization of cluster failed, variables only process by code (not configuration) should be reset as default (in my case default is false).

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**

- variable `spec.storage.useAllDevices` has to be defined as `true`.
- put another error in your `CephCluster` manifest (for exemple don't set `spec.storage.config` triggers an error)
- apply your manifest
- see that initialization failed
- get your manifest correct and re-apply it
- "using all devices in more than one namespace is not supported" error happen.
<!-- Please let us know any circumstances for reproduction of your bug. -->

**Logs**

(first error was because spec.storage.config is null)

`2020-01-07 13:06:21.995063 E | op-cluster: failed to update cluster rook-ceph status: CephCluster.ceph.rook.io "rook-ceph" is invalid: spec.storage.config: Invalid value: "null": spec.storage.config in body must be of type object: "null"`

(then as explained above, I updated spec and added config field then this happened):

`2020-01-08 09:57:24.629863 I | op-cluster: Update event for uninitialized cluster rook-ceph. Initializing...
2020-01-08 09:57:24.629892 I | op-cluster: CephCluster rook-ceph status: Error. using all devices in more than one namespace is not supported
2020-01-08 09:57:24.664597 E | op-cluster: failed to configure local ceph cluster. using all devices in more than one namespace is not supported
2020-01-08 09:57:24.665640 I | op-cluster: Update event for uninitialized cluster rook-ceph. Initializing...
2020-01-08 09:57:24.665651 I | op-cluster: CephCluster rook-ceph status: Error. using all devices in more than one namespace is not supported
2020-01-08 09:57:24.676999 E | op-cluster: failed to configure local ceph cluster. using all devices in more than one namespace is not supported
`

**Environment**:
* OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release):
Container Linux by CoreOS 2345.0.0
* Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
4.19.87-coreos
* Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
online
* Rook version (use `rook version` inside of a Rook Pod):
v1.1.2 (but this part of code doesn't change in latest (v1.2.1)
* Storage backend version (e.g. for ceph do `ceph -v`):
ceph version 14.2.4 - nautilus (stable)
* Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
1.16.2
* Kubernetes cluster type (e.g. Tectonic, GKE, OpenShift):
baremetal

**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**

When only deploying an external cluster with rook(so we have no previous internal ceph cluster) in the rook-ceph namespaces we get the following error when deploying the RGW services( object-openshift.yaml or object.yaml):

[root@helper ~]# oc get pods | grep rgw

It seems that the cm rook-config-override doesn't get created by default like when we do a normal/internal deploy of ceph-rook.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4882: Tolerations from Cluster CR are not included in OSD Deployments

Issue description:
**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**
Tolerations which are configured in the Cluster CRD [as suggested in the Rook Docs](https://rook.io/docs/rook/v1.2/ceph-cluster-crd.html#placement-configuration-settings) are not included in the OSD Deployments. Instead, only (built-in?) tolerations for NoExecute conditions are included. In addition, the prepare jobs are started without any tolerations at all.

**Expected behavior:**
The Tolerations I configure in the Cluster CRD are merged with the built-in NoExecute tolerations of the OSDs themselves and included in the prepare jobs.

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**
1. Create a k8s cluster with workers with the ``role=storage`` label and a ``role=storage:NoSchedule`` taint.
2. Deploy Rook up to the Operator step
3. Configure a Cluster CRD with NoSchedule tolerations for the ``role=storage`` taint and nodeAffinity for the ``role=storage`` label, [as documented here](https://rook.io/docs/rook/v1.2/ceph-cluster-crd.html#placement-configuration-settings). In addition, configure the node and pod affinity in [the storage device class](https://rook.io/docs/rook/v1.2/ceph-cluster-crd.html#storage-class-device-sets).
4. Observe that the OSD prepare jobs fail to schedule: "0/9 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 6 node(s) didn't match node selector."
5. If you remove the taint from one of the nodes, the prepare jobs will schedule and execute; all OSDs will be scheduled to that node, because the OSD deployments lack the appropriate tolerations.

Issue #5073: Failed to start the resizer container due to misinterpretation of the cephcsi version

Issue description:
<!-- **Are you in the right place?**

**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**
The csi-rbdplugin-provisioner pod failed to start the resizer container due to mis-interpretation of the cephcsi version if the image registry includes ":" as part of name.  i.e., "bcmt-registry:5000/csi/cephcsi:v2.0.0".

**Expected behavior:**
The cephcsi version can be parsed differently to get the correct cephcsi version. So the resizer container can be started as part of csi-rbdplugin-provisioner pod.
Would like to know if there's any workaround without changing the registry name.

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**
<!-- Please let us know any circumstances for reproduction of your bug. -->
Deploy rook 1.2.5/ceph14.2.7 and cephcsi v2.0.0 version. The cephcsi's image registry has ":" as part of its name. The csi-rbdplugin-provisioner pod starts with 5 containers without resizer container.

The code failed at file " ./operator/ceph/csi/spec.go" line 230.  The version should be in the last element: [len(csiPluginImage)-1], not necessarily the hardcoded 2nd element.
Any possible to include the above code change? The similar issue happened at line 222 as well.
```
csiPluginImage := strings.Split(CSIParam.CSIPluginImage, ":")
        // as ceph-csi v2.x.x support resizer, enable it
        if len(csiPluginImage) > 1 {
                **if strings.HasPrefix(csiPluginImage[1], "v2.") {**
                        tp.EnableResizer = true
                }
        }
```

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #5547: replace commitlint bot with commitlint github action

Issue description:
commitlint bot is now deprecated https://github.com/z0al/commitlint-bot, it hasn't been updated for years and its maintainers recommend going with https://github.com/apps/semantic-pull-requests instead. Which seems to be a bit more powerful.  commitlint was lacking flexibility and it seems nobody understood it despite our various efforts.

My idea is to go with semantic-pull-requests, which will work with basic rules and requires proper PR as well as commit semantic. It does not print any comment in the PR, the PR status check will be red and it will indicate the reason.

One addition I'm thinking about is to use mergify to react on a failure of this check and post a proper message (written by us) that contains what we except. See the example of the rule: https://doc.mergify.io/examples.html#request-for-action.

Semantic example https://github.com/leseb/Scripts/pull/6 where it's complaining about the title of PR being incorrect. We can decide between PR and/or commit.

Issue #4907: Do not block OBC request handling on OBC deletion

Issue description:
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**
Deletion of an OBC whose OB has many entries blocks handling of subsequent OBC requests.

**Expected behavior:**
OBCs are deleted asynchronously.

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**
1. Create an OBC.
2. Populate the OB owned by the OBC with several million entries.
3. Delete the OBC.
4. In another session, create another OBC.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #6111: Ceph operator iterating over all Nodes instead of just OSD placement valid Nodes

Issue description:
**Is this a bug report or feature request?**
* Bug Report

**Deviation from expected behavior:**

The operator is iterating over all Nodes on startup and not just the Nodes which are valid for OSDs, see https://github.com/rook/rook/blob/master/pkg/operator/ceph/cluster/watcher.go#L81.

It is operating over all Nodes because Kubernetes sends all objects as "Created" when a watch is created.

**Expected behavior:**

The operator to only iterate over the Nodes on startup that are valid for OSDs placement.

**How to reproduce it (minimal and precise):**

1. Not having a `all` placement which keeps Rook Ceph on the nodes with OSDs.
	* (Optional) Remove `all` placement from CephCluster object.
1. (Re-)Start the operator.
1. Check the operator logs, it will begin logging out an  "error" per node (without OSDs) but continue normally (error is correctly handled) with the iteration and in the end, the Nodes watch loop.

**Environment**:
* Rook version (use `rook version` inside of a Rook Pod): v1.4.1
* Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): `v1.18.6`
* Kubernetes cluster type (e.g. Tectonic, GKE, OpenShift): Bare metal

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: ceph: operator should only "watch" OSD placement nodes
PR description:
**Description of your changes:**

This change is the first part to improve the watch OSD nodes logic in
the Rook Ceph operator.
This commit changes the "is node valid check" to use the OSD placement
instead of the all placement. The OSD placement is "merged" with the
all placement already.

Second step will be to skip the first "iteration" of the "nodes added"
events and then start the actual watch logic.

Partially resolves #6111.

Signed-off-by: Alexander Trost <galexrt@googlemail.com>

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #247: multi-cluster weighted routing rule

Issue description:
Right now it's clumsy if the user wants to have a routing rule that matches and then sends traffic to a number of upstream clusters on a % basis. We should support this directly both via static percentages as well as runtime override of the percentages.

The rule might look something like:

```
{
...
"weighted_clusters:" [
  { "name": "cluster1", "weight": 33 },
  { "name": "cluster2", "weight": 33 },
  { "name": "cluster3", "weight": 33 },
]
}
```

Need to also specify what the rule would look like with runtime overrides. Open so to suggestions here.

cc @rshriram

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Support for multiple weighted clusters in routing
PR description:
[apologies for the delayed turn around for this feature].

This PR provides an intuitive way of specifying cluster weights, when a particular route is backed by two or more clusters. Instead of using the existing Runtime style probability specification, users can group related clusters under a single weighted_clusters block with % weights assigned to each cluster.

Please refer to #247 for more details.

The current PR is missing documentation. Will add that in a day or so. TLDR:
In the routing config, you can have either the `cluster` key or the `weighted_clusters` key.
The `weighted_clusters` is of the following format:
```json
"weighted_clusters" : {
"runtime_key_prefix" : "foo",
"clusters" : [{ "name" : "cluster-name", "weight" : N },
...
]}
```
where N is an integer from 0 to 100. It determines the proportion of request traffic to be sent to the target cluster. The sum of all weights in the weighted cluster should be equal to 100.

*On runtime support for weighted clusters:* If we wish to validate the weights provided by the user (as we do it currently), it is not exactly clear how the weights would be validated (i.e. sum of weights == 100) if runtime support were to be enabled for a weighted cluster. My current inclination is to skip runtime support altogether for weighted_clusters. With the addition of RDS, a user can combine weighted cluster and RDS to dynamically change weights. It may not occur instantaneously (as it depends on the RDS poll interval).

Fixes #247

@mattklein123 @ccaraman

p.s.: For reviewing this PR, please do not look at the individual commits. Instead, I suggest looking at config_impl.h|cc as one change set and then config_impl_test.cc as another change set.

PR title: perf: optimize generation of UUIDs.
PR description:
This change includes two improvements:

1) Prefetching 2048 bytes of randomness (per thead) at a time.

2) Using char[] instead of std::string for bytes-to-hex conversion.

The UUID generation is ~16x faster (~90x faster than before commit

traffic on localhost is only ~5%, because it's already on par with

    UUIDUtilsTest.benchmark:  6,638 ms
    wrk    -c 100 w/o hpack: 83,987 req/s

    UUIDUtilsTest.benchmark:  1,371 ms

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #1873: Envoy API proto build rules via Bazel native proto support

Issue description:
Bazel has _some_ support for generating protos via its inbuilt `proto_library` and `cc_proto_library` rules today (see https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/be/protocol-buffer.html). We've so far been using the imported rules for `cc_proto_library` etc from https://github.com/google/protobuf/blob/master/protobuf.bzl, because we wanted a high degree of control over the protobuf compiler and runtime (associated largely with our former approach to external dep build for protobuf prior to #1682).

We may now be able to switch to native support, which has the advantage that the `proto_library` rule provides language neutral support for management of transitive proto dependencies. This is useful when doing things like adding additional proto rules to generate constraint validation code (https://github.com/lyft/protoc-gen-validate) and documentation (#1866), since you can avoid horrible hacks like https://github.com/lyft/protoc-gen-validate/blob/master/bazel/go_proto_library.bzl.diff. This might also make it simpler to add support for additional languages (e.g. Go), since the transitivity management is factored out.

It's a bit unclear to me how mature the support is in native Bazel for the latest protobuf toolchain, so creating this tracking issue to investigate. https://blog.bazel.build/2017/02/27/protocol-buffers.html describes how to get started. One thing we'll need to do is rename our protobuf repo to `@com_google_protobuf`.

@jmillikin-stripe @lizan for comment. @rodaine for PGV applications.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: bazel: switch to native proto_library/cc_proto_library.
PR description:
Envoy repo side change following https://github.com/envoyproxy/data-plane-api/pull/201.

This allows us to drop the custom patch for protobuf. One not so nice thing is that the native
cc_proto_library doesn't play nice with the hack we had in place to get at generated .pb.h files via
the "Envoy canonical include path", i.e. common/ instead of source/common/. There aren't that many
places this is an issue, but it's a bit uglier.

Also switched back to `-fPIC`; recent versions of Bazel seem to avoid doing multiple redundant builds that used to plague us when PIC was enabled.

Fixes #1873.

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #2141: Stats broken out by response code and class lead to duplicated metrics in tagged stats formats

Issue description:
*Description*:
Stats such as upstream_rq which are broken out by response code (e.g. 404) and response code class (e.g. 4xx) lead to duplicated data in metrics.
For example:
```
cluster.FOO.upstream_rq_403: 2
cluster.FOO.upstream_rq_404: 1726
cluster.FOO.upstream_rq_4xx: 1728
```
Currently leads to the following in Prometheus format:
```
cluster_upstream_rq{cluster_name="FOO",envoy_response_code="403"} 2
cluster_upstream_rq{cluster_name="FOO",envoy_response_code="404"} 1726
cluster_upstream_rq{cluster_name="FOO",envoy_response_code_class="4xx"} 1728
```
Which means that aggregates over the cluster_upstream_rq metric are meaningless (e.g. sum(cluster_upstream_rq) = 3456).

The output should be metrics with both a response_code and response_code_class label:
```
cluster_upstream_rq{cluster_name="FOO",envoy_response_code="403",envoy_response_code_class="4xx"} 2
cluster_upstream_rq{cluster_name="FOO",envoy_response_code="404",envoy_response_code_class="4xx"} 1726
```
Or, alternatively, the response_code_class labels could be dropped entirely since they can be calculated by Prometheus from the response_code labels if needed.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: tag extraction: remove duplicate names for response code class metrics
PR description:
*Description*:
All stats that end with `*rq_5xx` and `*rq_500` (for example) were being mapped to the same `tag_extracted_name`: `*rq`, which is expected to be a unique identifier for a particular stat in order for downstream systems to take advantage of tag extraction.  Since two logical stats were being collapsed to the same name, this uniqueness was violated (see #2141 for details).  This change updates the mapped name and tag value of the `*rq_5xx` case.  The tag value becomes `5` rather than `5xx` and the `tag_extracted_name` becomes `*rq_xx` (these choices are due to the current limitations of the regex extraction system).

Future work: add some complexity to the tag extraction regex system to allow the user to inject strings that are not present in the canonical string name into the `tag_extracted_name`.  However, this fix should be good for differentiating these two sets of stats for the time being.

Fixes #2141

*Risk Level*: Low

*Testing*:
Updated existing tag extraction tests to ensure that updated regexes work as expected.

Issue #2782: NO_TRAFFIC_INTERVAL constant causes deployments to needlessly take at least a minute

Issue description:
We use AWS load balancer in front of envoy, which is used as a sidecar. Envoy proxies all external traffic into our local application.

When the application comes up for the first time, envoy waits 60 seconds between healthcheck attempts because of NO_TRAFFIC_INTERVAL constant, which is used in case there's no external traffic into the cluster.

However, there can be no external traffic at this point, as for it to come, the healthcheck needs to become healthy at least once.

What can we optimize to workaround this? Ideally, we'd like to be able to tune the NO_TRAFFIC_INTERVAL timeout ourselves to disable this behavior.

Here's the config we use, note the ```envoy.health_check``` http_filter that is the endpoint that is served to AWS load balancer.

```static_resources:
  clusters:
    name: local_tomcat
    connect_timeout: 0.1s
    health_checks:
    - healthy_threshold: 2
      http_health_check:
        path: "/app/status"
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      unhealthy_threshold: 3
    hosts:
    - socket_address:
        address: 127.0.0.1
        port_value: 8080
    lb_policy: LEAST_REQUEST
    type: STATIC
  listeners:
  - address:
      socket_address:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port_value: 9443
    filter_chains:
    - filters:
      - name: envoy.http_connection_manager
        config:
          http_filters:
            - name: envoy.health_check
              config:
                cluster_min_healthy_percentages:
                  local_tomcat:
                    value: 100
                endpoint: "/healthz"
                pass_through_mode: false
            - name: envoy.router
          route_config:
            name: localhost_proxy
            virtual_hosts:
            - domains: "*"
              name: localhost_proxy
              routes:
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                route:
                  cluster: local_tomcat
                  timeout: 60s

      tls_context: {...}
    name: localhost_proxy
```

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: Add no traffic interval config
PR description:
Add no traffic interval config

This PR adds a new "no traffic interval config". The "no traffic interval" is
a special health check interval that is used when a cluster has never
had traffic routed to it. This lower interval allows cluster information
to be kept up to date, without sending a potentially large amount of active
health checking traffic for no reason. Once a cluster has been used for traffic
routing, Envoy will shift back to using the standard health check interval
that is defined.

$ git add empty-file
$ git commit -a -m "testing."
$ git log --pretty=oneline
35931e6a89f38fe8ad3334e1d13bf056e2464f4d testing.
97b69ce6a507471180c0585b6742c627962b433b test: automatically registering integration ports from listener names (#2536)
...

$ rm bazel-bin/source/exe/envoy-static
$ bazel build //source/exe:envoy-static
$ bazel-bin/source/exe/envoy-static --version

bazel-bin/source/exe/envoy-static  version: 97b69ce6a507471180c0585b6742c627962b433b/1.6.0-dev/Clean/DEBUG

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #3569: tracing: Health check filter only prevents sampling of root span

Issue description:
*Description*:

When the health check filter is used, any invocation that matches the health check path causes the root span to not be sampled, but the sampled flag is not be propagated to subsequent services. The subsequent services (or child spans) should also not be sampled.

*Repro steps*:

* Change to the `examples/jaeger-tracing` folder
* Edit the `front-envoy-jaeger.yaml` to update the `http_filter` to be:
```
          http_filters:
          - name: envoy.health_check
            config:
              endpoint: "/trace/1"
              pass_through_mode: true
          - name: envoy.router
            config:
               start_child_span: true
```
* Start the example using `docker-compose up --build -d`
* Send a request using `curl -v localhost:8000/trace/1`
* Access the Jaeger UI at endpoint `http://localhost:16686`
You should see a single trace, which when selected will show something like:
![envoy-hc-traced](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/164562/41096269-013c5a04-6a4c-11e8-9bda-d37b9d9afc17.png)

The root span has not been reported due to the classification as a health check, but the sampled status has not been passed to the child span created in the proxy, or on to the subsequent `service1`, etc.

The same applies if the `start_child_span` is false, the spans for `service1` and `service2` are created - this time with `service1` as the root span - so indicates that the root span in the ingress is being created but not reported, but the sampled flag is not being propagated to the child span or subsequent services.

Also the other strange thing is that if the `X-B3-Sampled` header is supplied (whether with 0 or 1 value), it does not cause a trace to be created.

A pull request was created to resolve it:

PR title: tracing: don't sample requests classified as a health check
PR description:
*Description*:
This PR fixes #3569.

There are two separate problems.

* The reason that the root span was not being reported for the health check is that if a request was classified as a health check, it didn't finish the span. So all spans were still being created and considered sampled.

* The second issue was that when the sampling decision is being made, the health check filter had not yet been invoked, and therefore was not being taken into account. Therefore I exposed the `setSampled` method in the abstract `Span` API and enabled the health check filter to explicitly set whether the span is sampled.

The issue is that potentially by the time the filter is invoked, other filters may have created child spans. However I am not sure how else we can use logic executed mid stream (i.e. the health check filter) to influence the sampling decision.

The other issue is that normally the sampling decision is made when a root span for a trace is being created. With this PR, it is possible that an existing trace will have a subpart of the trace (i.e. the part  considered to be the health check) not sampled, while the remainder of the trace is still reported. Let me know if I haven't clearly explained this, as might be confusing :)

*Risk Level*: Low

*Testing*:
Needs tests - currently just looking for feedback on the fix.

none.

none.

Issue description:

A repository contains the following reported issue:

Issue #4710: Stronger API semantic versioning guarantees

Issue description:
Today, we use proto namespaces to express versioning, with `v2alpha` reserved for experimental protos and `v2` for stable.

By "stable", we mean that protos are subject to the normal restrictions on wire-level backwards compatibility for proto, see https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/master/api/STYLE.md, and that any field removal or semantic change is subject to Envoy's breaking change policy, see https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/blob/master//CONTRIBUTING.md#breaking-change-policy.

So far, most field removals have been done in support of alternative API features with supersets of removed functionality. This allows config translators in xDS generation pipelines to continue to function.

There are two problems we have with the above:
1. There is no stated API guarantee that we won't remove support for features at the semantic level across Envoy releases. This means that if Envoy consumer X offers feature A in their own APIs to their customers with a guarantee of N years support, and Envoy turns down A in a 3 month cycle deprecation cycle, then the Envoy consumer can't offer its stronger API guarantees to its customers.
2. It's difficult to reason about API status based on Envoy release version, since this is not expressed directly in the protos or wire format.

I think we should have a stronger policy statement for (1), e.g. "you can only remove in favor of superset capabilities that can be mechanically translated to" and for (2) start to make use of `.v3` or `.v2.1` etc. to version at proto level.

In this case we have 4 hosts that all have equal weighting (2 in each locality, with same locality weighting and same priority):
